articles.title: As France's problems multiply, so do its presidential hopefuls
articles.summary: France's 2027 presidential field has grown to more than 30 declared or prospective contenders as traditional party structures weaken. Olympic judo champion Teddy Riner, former prime minister Dominique de Villepin and Cannes mayor David Lisnard are among recent entrants. Reuters says Marine Le Pen and Jean-Luc Mélenchon remain leading figures in polls, so the crowded field has yet to dislodge the frontrunners.

articles.title: Kenyan cult leader serving 200 years for murder convicted of terrorism-related charges
articles.summary: A Kenyan magistrate convicted Paul Mackenzie of organised criminal activity, radicalisation and facilitating terrorism linked to the Shakahola mass killings. Mackenzie is already serving 200 years for murdering nearly 200 children and was separately convicted of child cruelty and assault the previous day. He pleaded not guilty to the terrorism charges; a lawyer said he plans to appeal. A manslaughter ruling was still pending.

articles.title: Guinea-Bissau delays elections, extending military-led transition a year after coup
articles.summary: Guinea-Bissau's military-led authorities moved presidential and legislative elections from December 2026 to November 2028, saying the country lacks the resources and conditions for a credible vote. The army seized power in November 2025, disrupting an election and promising a one-year transition. The extension deepens uncertainty over a return to civilian rule and runs against regional calls for a short, transparent transition.

articles.title: Iraq closes two border crossings in Kurdistan region with Syria and Iran
articles.summary: Iraqi border forces closed the al-Waleed crossing with Syria and the Bashta crossing with Iran, both in territory administered by the Kurdistan Regional Government. The closures follow a court ruling allowing federal forces to deploy along all international borders and a prime ministerial order to take over KRG-run crossings. Baghdad says the moves strengthen central control; Kurdish authorities' response and practical effects remain developing.

articles.title: Sweden's Centre leader backs right-wing prime minister, in major shift
articles.summary: Sweden's Centre Party leader Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist recommended that the party back a minority government led by caretaker Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson, a sharp shift after campaigning for a centre-left coalition. Lawmakers are due to vote Monday, and the Centre Party's governing council must still approve the recommendation. The move could break a post-election deadlock, but the internal decision was not unanimous.

articles.title: Co-leader of Germany's AfD criticises planned talks with Russian envoy
articles.summary: Germany's AfD co-leader Alice Weidel criticised plans by party lawmaker Markus Frohnmaier to meet Kremlin business envoy Kirill Dmitriev in Abu Dhabi to discuss trade and a possible return of Russian gas supplies. Weidel said the party has no mandate for such negotiations and would not join the talks. The dispute exposes tensions inside AfD as Moscow seeks support for restoring energy ties with Germany.

articles.title: Mexico urges Asian trade partners to crack down on tariff dodging
articles.summary: Mexico urged Asian trade partners to strengthen checks against goods being rerouted through third countries to evade tariffs, as Washington presses for tighter rules on Chinese components in North American supply chains. Economy Minister Marcelo Ebrard called for better origin tracing and enforcement while Mexico reviews the USMCA. Mexico has already raised tariffs on some imports, including Chinese goods, by as much as 50%.

articles.title: US chip curbs will slow Asia data-center investment, Fitch says
articles.summary: Fitch Ratings expects tighter U.S. chip-export controls to slow and reshape Asia-Pacific data-center investment, especially for operators dependent on Chinese customers and advanced Nvidia processors. Projects with uncertain chip access could face delays, weaker utilization, lower pricing and tighter lending. Fitch said investment may shift toward facilities with diversified customers and secure supplies; the scale of disruption will depend on licensing and eligibility decisions.

articles.title: China's Weimob plans own GPU cluster with Nvidia's RTX PRO 5500
articles.summary: Chinese commerce-software provider Weimob plans to deploy about 5,000 Nvidia RTX PRO 5500 GPUs in a cluster for multimodal computing, image and video generation, and marketing-content tools. The workstation-grade chips are among the most capable Nvidia products available to Chinese buyers under U.S. export controls. Weimob may lease spare capacity to other firms, but flagged supply, deployment and demand risks.

articles.title: Trump moves to replace Texas judicial nominee opposed by Senator Cornyn
articles.summary: President Donald Trump is moving to replace Texas judicial nominee T. Elliot Gaiser after Republican Senator John Cornyn blocked the nomination from advancing, citing vetting concerns and Gaiser's ties outside the state. The White House has submitted partial paperwork for former prosecutor Steve Fahey for the Dallas judgeship. The switch reflects a broader scramble to confirm nominees before Democrats take Senate control in January.

articles.title: Shanghai Chinese Communist Party secretary Chen Jining, a rising star, becomes latest victim of Xi's endless purges
articles.summary: Shanghai party chief Chen Jining was placed under investigation for alleged serious violations of discipline and law, a formula commonly associated with corruption probes. He is the fourth Politburo member to fall since the body was formed in 2022, an unusually rapid pace ahead of the party's 2027 congress. The reasons remain undisclosed; analysts point to a wider purge and uncertainty over elite succession.

articles.title: Kremlin accuses Ukraine of trying to widen conflict zone to Mediterranean and Baltic seas
articles.summary: The Kremlin accused Ukraine of widening the war after Ukrainian maritime drones struck Russian-linked vessels in the Mediterranean and Baltic regions. Spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the attacks could alarm coastal states and NATO; Libya and Italy condemned the operation, while Norway urged caution. The accusation follows a joint Trump-Rutte warning against escalation, but reflects Moscow's account of events rather than an independent finding.

articles.title: Argentina's Senate poised to suspend primaries, boosting Milei's re-election bid
articles.summary: Argentina's Senate began debating a bill to suspend the 2027 primary elections, cut public funding for parties and remove the mandatory presidential debate. President Javier Milei's government says it has enough support for passage, though the lower house would still need to approve the measure. Supporters cite lower costs; critics say removing primaries would weaken democratic safeguards and could aid Milei's reelection bid.

articles.title: Turkish elections to be held in 2028, ruling alliance agrees on Erdogan candidacy, vice president says
articles.summary: Turkey's Vice President Cevdet Yilmaz said elections will be held in 2028, though the date could move one or two months earlier than the scheduled May vote. He also said the ruling alliance has agreed that President Recep Tayyip Erdogan should be its candidate again. The remarks clarify the governing bloc's plans but do not establish the final election date or resolve any legal and political hurdles.

articles.title: Iran's supreme leader urges Guards-linked Basij volunteers to broaden social reach
articles.summary: Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei urged the Basij, a nationwide volunteer force tied to the Revolutionary Guards, to recruit supporters beyond its formal membership and broaden its social role. The force helps organize pro-government rallies, enforce social codes and suppress protests. Khamenei has remained out of public view since succeeding his father; officials cite security concerns, while the country faces sanctions and economic strain.

articles.title: Dutch groups ask court to halt Meta smart glasses sales over privacy concerns
articles.summary: Dutch consumer and digital-rights groups asked an Amsterdam court to halt sales of Meta's AI-powered Ray-Ban glasses, arguing they enable covert recording and violate European privacy law. They also seek limits on using footage to train AI. Meta denies processing European images or using them for training, and says a recording light alerts bystanders. A ruling is expected by December 24 and could influence wider European policy.

articles.title: Polish defence ministry to sign agreement with Palantir on Friday
articles.summary: Poland's defence ministry said it will sign a Friday agreement to buy Palantir software using artificial intelligence to support military decision-making. The ministry disclosed no contract value or technical details. Poland began cooperating with the U.S. data-analytics company in 2025 under a memorandum covering AI, information technology and cybersecurity, making the new deal a further step in defence digitisation.

articles.title: Mexico seeking talks with US on SpaceX airspace use
articles.summary: Mexico is seeking talks with U.S. aviation authorities about permits for SpaceX to use Mexican airspace and the possibility of relocating launch operations, President Claudia Sheinbaum said. Mexico says debris from Texas launches has reached its territory and raised environmental and airspace concerns. SpaceX says it sent specialists to help identify debris and cited independent tests finding no chemical, biological or toxicological risk.

articles.title: Iberdrola scraps plans for €427 million green ammonia project in Portugal
articles.summary: Iberdrola cancelled its planned €427 million Green Ammonia Express plant at Sines, Portugal, after reviewing investment priorities. The project was designed to use 137 megawatts of electrolysers to produce about 95,000 tonnes of green ammonia annually for fertilizer and chemical makers. The company said it remained at a preliminary stage; weak demand and high costs have pressured Europe's low-carbon ammonia sector.

articles.title: LATAM Brasil says initial E195-E2 route sales running above expectations
articles.summary: LATAM Brasil says initial sales for routes operated by new Embraer E195-E2 jets are exceeding expectations, CEO Jerome Cadier told Reuters. The airline added six Brazilian destinations and increased frequencies on ten domestic routes while retaining its 24-aircraft order. Cadier said it will take about six months to assess the strategy; higher fuel costs and a strong dollar remain pressures, but the carrier has not changed its growth plans.

articles.title: Germany's IG Metall reaches wage deal with employers
articles.summary: Germany's IG Metall union reached a wage deal with employers covering 3.7 million workers in the metal and electrical industries. The agreement provides increases of 2.0% from May 2027 and 2.3% from April 2028, plus one-off payments of €150–€450 depending on company returns. The pilot deal is expected to set a pattern nationwide, after 24-hour strikes amid pressure on German automakers and exporters.

articles.title: Brazil not ready yet for household debt-service cap, central bank official says
articles.summary: Brazil's central bank says the country is not ready to cap household debt-service ratios because informal income and varied credit-card use make borrowers' obligations difficult to measure. The bank is consulting on a standardized methodology while monitoring rising debt; household debt service excluding mortgages reached 26.7% in August. New credit rules, including gradual limits for revolving-card users, could affect about 20 million people.

articles.title: Brazil's finance minister to meet Lula on further fiscal measures
articles.summary: Brazil Finance Minister Dario Durigan plans to meet President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva to discuss further steps to restrain public spending. Durigan said the government should use its congressional strength to revisit tax exemptions on some financial products and consider corporate-tax reform, potentially offsetting payroll taxes. The talks signal continued fiscal-tightening debate, but no specific measure or legislative timetable was announced.

articles.title: Former IOC vice-president and trailblazer Anita DeFrantz dies at 74
articles.summary: Anita DeFrantz, an Olympic rowing bronze medallist and pioneering International Olympic Committee leader, has died aged 74, the IOC said. She captained the U.S. rowing team at the 1976 Montreal Games and became the first African American and first American woman to join the IOC in 1986. She later became its first female vice-president and chaired its Women and Sport Commission for nearly two decades.

articles.title: Germany must prepare for two more difficult years with Trump, DIW's Fratzscher says
articles.summary: German economic researcher Marcel Fratzscher warned that Germany should prepare for two difficult years under President Donald Trump, citing tariffs, geopolitical conflicts, energy costs and weak private investment. He expects growth above 1% in 2027 but says government spending, not households or businesses, will drive it. Fratzscher also argued the European Central Bank may need two or three rate increases next year to protect credibility.

articles.title: Settlers smash foundations of Palestinian family's homes in West Bank
articles.summary: Reuters reporters saw foundations of two Palestinian family homes damaged by settlers in Jaloud in the occupied West Bank, after the family had been displaced and blocked from returning despite a court order. Israel's military condemned the attack and said it was investigating. U.N. figures cited by Reuters record an average of 53 settler attacks weekly in 2026; rights groups say most investigations close without indictments.

articles.title: China Railway Resources Group plans $600 million investment in Zimbabwe gold mines
articles.summary: China Railway Resources Group signed an agreement to explore investing up to $600 million with Zimbabwe-focused Duration Gold to revive and expand four gold mines. The proposed partnership covers Vubachikwe, Gaika, Athens and Royal Family, and may bring financing, engineering and AI-based mining technology. Zimbabwe produced a record 46.7 tonnes of gold in 2025 as higher prices attracted investment; the agreement is not yet a completed funding commitment.

articles.title: OPEC+ likely to roll over oil output targets for Q1 as capacity disputes persist
articles.summary: OPEC+ is likely to keep current oil-production targets through at least the first quarter of 2027 when ministers meet Sunday, two sources told Reuters. Disagreements over capacity assessments by Iraq and Kazakhstan, alongside disruption from the Iran war, complicate quota decisions. No decision has been made. Forecasts of a large global surplus also weigh on prices, while members debate how to distribute production allowances.

articles.title: UK man found guilty of attempted murder charges over mass train stabbing
articles.summary: A British court convicted Anthony Williams of 14 counts of attempted murder over a 2025 mass stabbing on a London-bound train and four earlier attacks. Williams had admitted carrying out the stabbings but denied intending to kill. Ten people were attacked on the train; no one died. He is expected to be sentenced in early 2027. Police said the case was not treated as terrorism.

articles.title: Ukraine says North Korea temporarily halted missile shipments to ally Russia
articles.summary: Ukraine's military intelligence agency claims North Korea temporarily halted some weapons cooperation with Russia, including KN-23 missile and artillery-shell shipments, after a dispute over Moscow's approach to tensions with South Korea. Reuters could not independently verify the account or the statements attributed to officials, and Russia and North Korea did not respond. Pyongyang has supplied weapons to Moscow since 2023 and troops since 2024.

articles.title: EU may vote on authorising Tesla assisted-driving system at Dec 15 meeting
articles.summary: An EU meeting on December 15 may include a formal vote on authorising Tesla's assisted-driving system across the bloc, according to a new European Commission draft agenda. It is the first time the agenda explicitly mentions a possible vote. Approval would still require at least 15 of 27 member states representing 65% of the EU population; the earlier meeting was postponed from December 1.

articles.title: Australia delays final vote on gas reservation law for LNG exporters to February
articles.summary: Australia's Senate passed the second reading of a bill requiring LNG producers to reserve up to 20% of output for domestic use, but delayed the final vote until February 2027 after government amendments. The changes require the bill to return to the House before becoming law. The scheme is due to start in January 2028, with a regulator-set reserve intended to create a modest surplus; producers warn it could deter new supply investment.

articles.title: AP fact check: False maps exaggerate fallout from Iowa lead azide detonation
articles.summary: AP debunked viral maps that falsely showed lead-dust fallout spreading across the Midwest and East Coast. The Army's official projection showed a more limited plume moving southwest from the Iowa ammunition plant toward northern Missouri. EPA monitors detected no airborne lead around the site immediately after the blast, but agencies and independent researchers plan further testing of water, farms, homes and playgrounds. Whether any lead reached nearby properties remains unresolved.

articles.title: Saudi-led coalition says Houthis attacked Aramco's Jazan refinery
articles.summary: Saudi Arabia's coalition says Houthis attacked Aramco's Jazan refinery, designed to process up to 400,000 barrels of crude per day, and says it later destroyed a missile-launch platform in Hodeidah. The statement follows Houthi claims of attacks on Ras Tanura, Jeddah and Jazan; coalition forces reported drone interceptions but did not specify damage at Jazan. The escalation raises risks for Gulf energy infrastructure and Red Sea shipping.

articles.title: China, Japan, Taiwan and others push back against Trump's new tariff plans
articles.summary: China, Japan, Singapore and other U.S. trading partners protested proposed duties on 14 economies following a U.S. excess-capacity investigation. AP says China could face 20%, rising to 40%, Japan 15%, Singapore 20%, the EU 15% and Vietnam 35%; Taiwan expects to retain its previously negotiated 15% rate. The measures are expected early next year and could raise prices or deepen trade friction.

articles.title: World shares advance as Asian markets rebound and Europe rallies on easing tariff fears
articles.summary: Global shares advanced as Asian markets rebounded and European benchmarks gained 1.6%–1.9%, while U.S. markets closed for Thanksgiving. AI-linked shares helped Asia, though investors remained wary of tariffs and tech valuations. Before the holiday, the S&P 500 fell 0.3%, Nasdaq 0.6% and Dow rose 0.3%; Brent reached $91.09 amid Middle East supply concerns. Friday's shortened session is the next test.

articles.title: India's top court tightens food warning labels in new setback for industry
articles.summary: India's Supreme Court ordered separate front-of-pack warnings for high salt, sugar and fat, rejecting a single combined label. It criticised global companies for resisting warning labels in India while using them elsewhere, saying Indian consumers deserve comparable protection. The Food Safety and Standards Authority must implement separate hexagon warnings; companies will have one year to adjust after the final law is issued.

articles.title: ‘Unbelievable catch’: Motorbike passenger in Swat becomes cricket sensation
articles.summary: Mehran Khan, a 27-year-old amateur cricketer and government employee in Pakistan's Swat Valley, became an online sensation after taking a one-handed catch while riding on the back of a moving motorcycle. The ball had been hit beyond a local ground during a tournament. The clip spread widely, drew praise from Brett Lee and earned Khan a 10,000-rupee award.

articles.title: 1Password breached through hijacked employee GitHub account, customer names and emails stolen
articles.summary: 1Password said an attacker compromised an employee's corporate GitHub account, inserted malicious code into backend services and copied administrative records for an undisclosed subset of customers. Names, email addresses, account identifiers and some emailed invitation or recovery tokens were exposed; vault contents and their protection keys were not. The company lengthened email codes and said it found no evidence of account takeovers.

articles.title: After initial reluctance, Bulgaria says it's 'ready' to join €45 billion Ukraine loan
articles.summary: Bulgaria reversed its earlier reluctance and agreed to join the EU's proposed €45 billion Ukraine loan, but Prime Minister Rumen Radev said it would contribute only to the €20 billion civilian-budget portion, not the €25 billion military component. The loan is intended to cover about two-thirds of Kyiv's 2027 wartime deficit; Slovakia, Hungary and Czechia remain opposed or seek exemptions.

articles.title: AI agents used in five cyber attacks in Switzerland, government says
articles.summary: Switzerland's Federal Office for Cybersecurity said AI agents were used in five recent attacks on companies and critical-infrastructure operators. Four attacks succeeded and compromised systems, while three targeted operators included electricity, water or telecommunications providers, according to Swiss public broadcaster SRF. Authorities did not identify suspects or affected organizations and advised firms to strengthen protections and conduct regular security testing.

articles.title: As COP31 stalls, countries and companies rally around electrification
articles.summary: COP31 ended without agreement on fossil-fuel transition language or climate finance, while negotiators disputed carbon-capture provisions. Outside the talks, about 90 countries and more than 180 companies backed a voluntary goal to raise electricity's share of final energy use to 35% by 2035. Delivering the pledge will require modernized grids and more finance for developing countries, which receive a small share of transition funding.

articles.title: ECB turns to crisis veteran De Cos as new strains loom
articles.summary: EU leaders selected former Bank of Spain governor Pablo Hernández de Cos to succeed Christine Lagarde as European Central Bank president, with his term due to begin in February. Now head of the Bank for International Settlements, he is viewed as a pragmatic moderate and is expected to preserve policy continuity. His first major test may be financial strains in France and rising eurozone inflation.

articles.title: French cinema star Gérard Depardieu ordered to stand trial for rape and sexual assault
articles.summary: France's Paris Court of Appeal ordered Gérard Depardieu to stand trial over allegations that he raped and sexually assaulted actress Charlotte Arnould in 2018. The court dismissed allegations tied to a second alleged incident. Depardieu, 77, denies the charges and may challenge the ruling. The case follows a separate 2025 sexual-assault conviction that he stopped appealing earlier this month.

articles.title: French far-right leader Bardella faces fresh antisemitism accusations in media reports
articles.summary: French media published additional alleged 2013 chat messages attributed to National Rally leader Jordan Bardella, prompting renewed scrutiny ahead of next year's presidential election. Bardella categorically denied making antisemitic remarks. Reuters said it could not independently verify the chats; Le Monde reported authenticating them with Meta and confirming the source's identity. The allegations' political impact remains uncertain.

articles.title: Investors see rising risk of SoftBank default as pressure grows on AI bets
articles.summary: Investors' cost of insuring SoftBank debt climbed to a four-year high as markets questioned whether its heavy AI investments, including its OpenAI stake, can generate returns fast enough to service borrowing. Five-year credit-default-swap spreads rose above 534 basis points, implying a market-estimated default probability of 34.8%. That pricing signals heightened concern; it is not a prediction that a default will occur.

articles.title: Iraqi Kurds protest against Baghdad leader's moves to assert central control
articles.summary: Thousands of Iraqi Kurds protested against Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi's moves to take over oilfields controlled by Kurdish authorities and deploy federal forces along regional borders. Iraq's top court ruled Baghdad could station troops at international borders, but the Kurdish regional government rejected the measures. The dispute follows a separate crackdown on an Iran-aligned militia and revives long-running tensions over oil, territory and smuggling.

articles.title: Irish High Court refuses to sanction BAWAG acquisition of Permanent TSB
articles.summary: Ireland's High Court refused to approve BAWAG's proposed €1.6 billion acquisition of Permanent TSB because minority shareholders were not given a separate vote. The Irish government, which owns 57.5% of the bank, supported the sale, but the judge said the statutory meeting requirement left no discretion to approve it. The current transaction scheme cannot proceed as presented; the parties' next steps were not immediately clear.

articles.title: Kremlin brushes off reports of 700,000 Russian war deaths
articles.summary: Analyses of hacked Russian statistics data produced estimates of 470,000 to 700,000 Russian military deaths in the war against Ukraine, including missing troops believed killed but not formally recorded. The Kremlin declined to address the estimates and said only the Defence Ministry can publish official figures; Russia has not issued a comprehensive military death toll since 2022. The figures remain unconfirmed estimates.

articles.title: Meta battles political storm in India as Congress party sues, stages protests
articles.summary: India's Congress party sued Meta and the federal government, alleging automated takedowns are suppressing lawful political speech before state elections. The party says posts featuring Rahul Gandhi were blocked even when they were birthday greetings, tributes or a wedding invitation; Meta says it is complying with Indian law. Reuters reports restrictions exceeded 5.4 million items in the first half of 2026, compared with about 70,000 in all of 2025.

articles.title: Ministers have ‘failed to make the case’ for Heathrow third runway, MPs say
articles.summary: A UK parliamentary transport committee said ministers have not justified a proposed third runway at Heathrow, citing weak economic projections, climate incompatibility, air-quality and noise concerns, and no funded public-transport plan. The £33 billion expansion could add 276,000 flights annually, while modelling suggested only a 0.05% GDP boost. Heathrow and supporters dispute the assessment, arguing expansion is important for connectivity and jobs.

articles.title: Myanmar’s leader says country will refuse to fully comply with ICJ requirements
articles.summary: Myanmar's military-backed president said the government would reject parts of the International Court of Justice's legally binding ruling that found the country responsible for genocide against the Rohingya. The court ordered safe returns, reparations and prosecutions, but cannot enforce compliance directly; Security Council action could face vetoes. The U.K. recognized the genocide, sanctioned five officers and pledged £8 million in aid; the council is expected to discuss the ruling on Dec. 7.

articles.title: North Korean launderers turn to little-known crypto services to move Binance haul, say researchers
articles.summary: Researchers told Reuters that North Korean-linked launderers moved more than $600 million from the $6.3 billion Binance hack through THORChain and a coin-mixing service, complicating efforts to trace the stolen funds. The FBI had urged crypto services to block attacker wallets; North Korea denies involvement. Analysts say converting the remaining tokens into cash could take months or years, and some funds were frozen.

articles.title: Norway's Fjord Defence sees military spending boom outlasting Ukraine war, CEO says
articles.summary: Norwegian defence supplier Fjord Defence expects Europe's military spending surge to continue for five to 10 years, even if the war in Ukraine ends, its CEO told Reuters. More than 90% of the company's revenue is already unrelated to the conflict, and 70% of forecast 2027 sales were covered by orders. The company expects defence revenue to grow about 30% next year.

articles.title: Planet One to invest $933 million in Senegalese iron ore project
articles.summary: Planet One Group plans to invest $933 million in Senegal's Falémé iron-ore project, partnering with state-owned MIFERSO. The deposit is estimated to contain up to 600 million metric tons. A first $200 million phase would upgrade mining infrastructure, roads and rail, targeting annual output of 3–5 million tons within 12–18 months. China, India and African markets are potential buyers; the full project would be developed in stages.

articles.title: Thousands march across Spain against violence toward women before election
articles.summary: Thousands demonstrated in Madrid, Valencia, Barcelona and Seville on November 25 against gender-based violence, days before Spain's general election. Euronews reported that one large march was organized by a trans-inclusive coalition, while another group opposed to that approach held a separate protest. The rallies featured national political figures and took place as far-right Vox polled near 18%, making women's rights a campaign issue.

articles.title: Trump heads to Arizona next week for a high-stakes expansion of TSMC’s computer chip factories
articles.summary: President Donald Trump plans to visit Arizona on December 4 for the groundbreaking of the fifth phase of Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co.'s Phoenix expansion. TSMC has pledged $265 billion in U.S. chipmaking investment, including an additional $100 billion announced in July. The White House projects 10,000 direct jobs, while construction began under Joe Biden and also received support from the bipartisan CHIPS and Science Act.

articles.title: Trump says he'd like to see Putin 'pull back' military aggression in Europe
articles.summary: President Donald Trump said he wanted Vladimir Putin to end military aggression across Europe to help secure a quick settlement of the war in Ukraine. Trump referred to discussions with Putin in China and described the conflict as a 'complete bloodbath,' but did not specify which other territories he meant. The remarks add to U.S. pressure for negotiations while Russia's invasion and wider regional security concerns continue.

articles.title: US Marlboro maker Altria explores Imperial Brands takeover in Big Tobacco mega deal
articles.summary: Altria confirmed it is considering an all-cash offer for Imperial Brands and said it is discussing buying part of the British tobacco company with an unnamed third party. Imperial shares rose as much as 17.6%, valuing it at about £26.8 billion; Japan Tobacco was also reported to be weighing a bid. Altria must make a firm offer or withdraw by December 24; no deal is assured.

articles.title: Zelenskyy warns of imminent major Russian attack on Ukraine’s power grid
articles.summary: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned that Russia was preparing another major strike on Ukraine's energy infrastructure, logistics and critical services as winter approaches. He said Russian forces launched ballistic missiles and 113 drones overnight, with hits reported at 20 locations and crews restoring power in six regions. U.S.-mediated peace talks remain stalled over territory, despite envoy Jared Kushner's more optimistic assessment of Vladimir Putin's intentions.

articles.title: ‘It’s in quite a dark place’: why UK housebuilding is struggling
articles.summary: UK housebuilding faces high costs, tighter lending and weaker buyer demand, with projects paused and developers issuing profit warnings. London’s private-sector housing construction has fallen 84% since 2015; England’s annual completions dropped to about 190,000 in 2024–25. Analysts cited by The Guardian say the government could miss its 1.5-million-home target by roughly 500,000 by 2029, while construction insolvencies remain elevated.

articles.title: (3rd LD) N. Korea's Kim inspects nuclear material sites, calls for broader use of tactical nukes
articles.summary: Kim Jong Un visited a newly built weapons-grade nuclear-material production base, a nuclear-equipment facility and the Nuclear Weapons Institute, state media reported. He called for expanded nuclear-material output and broader use of tactical weapons across multiple missions, while accusing U.S. allies of expanding nuclear cooperation. The facilities’ locations and production figures were not disclosed; the claims could not be independently verified.

articles.title: A Chinese consumer advocate is stranded in South Korea as a crackdown in China targets campaigners
articles.summary: Chinese consumer-rights advocate Wang Hai is stranded in South Korea with his wife and two children after fleeing a crackdown on people accused of making 'malicious compensation claims.' Wang says staff were detained, his offices closed and his accounts frozen; South Korea rejected the family's asylum applications and the U.S. revoked his tourist visa. He has appealed and is seeking resettlement elsewhere, while Beijing says it is unaware of his case.

articles.title: AI turmoil spurs risk-off mode as China government bond yield slides to record low
articles.summary: Investor caution over volatile AI shares has pushed China’s 10-year government-bond yield to a record low of 1.565% this month, while buyers have shifted toward dividend-paying stocks. The Shanghai Stock Exchange Dividend Index has gained about 7% year to date, outperforming several major domestic benchmarks. The move signals defensive positioning rather than confidence in a broad equity recovery.

articles.title: Air cargo demand from AI data centres shows no sign of slowing, SATS CEO says
articles.summary: SATS, the world's largest air-cargo handler, says demand tied to AI data-centre projects remains strong, with server racks and semiconductors driving cargo growth despite volatility in technology shares. CEO Kerry Mok told Reuters the trend continued through the peak season, while SATS volumes have outpaced the global industry's growth rate for 12 consecutive quarters. The outlook depends on continued AI infrastructure investment.

articles.title: AirBaltic offers crew exit, demotion or Papua New Guinea secondment
articles.summary: Latvia's airBaltic has offered some staff voluntary exits, demotions or secondments to Papua New Guinea's Air Niugini as it restructures under Chapter 11, Reuters reported from employee emails and sources. The carrier plans to cut 500–700 jobs and reduce its Airbus A220 fleet. AirBaltic says options comply with labour law; a union disputes that and says it was not consulted.

articles.title: Apple pulls MiniMax AI chatbot from App Store over child safety concerns
articles.summary: Apple removed MiniMax’s Talkie chatbot from its App Store worldwide after reports that AI characters sent sexually inappropriate or abusive messages to minors. Reuters says the app was rated for adults but relied partly on self-reported ages, raising questions about safeguards. Talkie had about 11 million monthly active users in October and was once a major revenue source for MiniMax; Apple and the company had not commented.

articles.title: At least 13 dead and 13 missing after illegal gold mine floods in Indonesia
articles.summary: Flooding at an unauthorised gold mine in West Java killed at least 13 workers and left 13 others missing, local rescue officials said. Hundreds of rescuers faced high water and unstable, poorly lit shafts about 100 metres deep. Authorities said the illegal operation delayed notification, as miners and residents initially tried to pump out water themselves. The search continued, and the toll could change.

articles.title: Australia's emissions fall but not fast enough to reach 2035 climate target
articles.summary: Australia's greenhouse-gas emissions fell 1.3% in the year to June 2026, but the Climate Change Authority says the pace must accelerate to meet the country's 2030 and 2035 targets. Renewables supplied a record 45.9% of electricity in the national market, while transport emissions edged up. Advisers estimate annual cuts of 25–30 million tonnes are needed over the next nine years.

articles.title: Australian court upholds rejection of proposed Hunter Valley biomass plant
articles.summary: New South Wales' Land and Environment Court dismissed Verdant Earth Technologies' appeal to convert the former Redbank coal station near Singleton into a 151-megawatt biomass plant. The proposal would have burned about 700,000 tonnes of material yearly; planners had rejected it over environmental impacts. The ruling leaves a proposed adjoining data-centre power partnership uncertain. The company says it is reviewing options and may pursue further legal steps.

articles.title: Bangchak shuts Bangkok refinery after fire; nine workers injured
articles.summary: Thailand's Bangchak shut all production units at its Phra Khanong refinery after a November 26 fire. Reuters reported nine workers injured; AP said three were in critical condition and nearby residents briefly evacuated. The blaze was extinguished in about 30 minutes, with officials reporting normal air quality within 3–4 km. The cause remains under investigation; a preliminary inquiry pointed to the hydrocracking unit.

articles.title: Bank of England to cut capital requirements for UK-focused lenders
articles.summary: The Bank of England plans to reduce capital requirements for large UK-focused lenders after concluding that overlapping rules made them hold more capital than historical losses justified. Proposed changes would cut requirements by 60 basis points for the largest domestic lenders and could add £175 billion in lending capacity across major banks. Regulators will consult on parts of the framework while retaining key resilience buffers.

articles.title: Bank of England warns of growing financial risks as AI borrowing jumps
articles.summary: The Bank of England warned that opaque, interconnected AI financing and increasingly capable models could amplify market, cyber and operational risks. Its report projects 6.5 million of seven million owner-occupier mortgages due to refinance by 2029 will see higher payments; the median increase is about £100 monthly. The Guardian reports around 430,000 borrowers could face rises exceeding £500 a month.

articles.title: Bank of Japan earnings fall as interest payments on reserves climb
articles.summary: Bank of Japan net income fell to 1.55 trillion yen in the first half of fiscal 2026 from 1.71 trillion a year earlier as higher rates increased payments on banks' excess reserves. The BOJ spent 1.91 trillion yen on reserve interest, exceeding income from government bonds, while ETF dividends partly offset the cost. The figures illustrate how policy normalisation is reshaping the central bank's balance sheet.

articles.title: Behind Alex Tuch's big night, Capitals best Flyers, end 5-game skid
articles.summary: Washington defeated Philadelphia 7–3, ending a five-game losing streak and handing the Flyers their first loss in four games. Alex Tuch scored once and assisted twice, while seven Capitals found the net and Logan Thompson made 18 saves. The teams traded early goals before Washington took control in the second period and added late insurance. The result was the Capitals’ second win over Philadelphia this season.

articles.title: Black Friday? No thanks, some brands say
articles.summary: Some brands are opting out of Black Friday to protect margins, push back against constant discounting or signal sustainability values. Italian fashion brand Pinko estimates the decision will cost about €2 million in revenue but says the profit hit is smaller. Analysts say discount fatigue and distrust of advertised savings make the strategy risky, though it can help retailers stand out.

articles.title: Blake Corum runs for 184 yards as Rams dump Packers, extend win streak
articles.summary: Blake Corum rushed for a career-high 184 yards and a touchdown as the Los Angeles Rams beat Green Bay 26–13 in the NFL's first Thanksgiving Eve game. The Rams extended their winning streak to five, while Jordan Love threw two interceptions and the Packers lost a second straight. Green Bay receiver Christian Watson left with a concussion after a hit that led to a Rams safety's ejection.

articles.title: Blue groper Ziggy missing after suspected Mollymook speargun attack
articles.summary: A protected eastern blue groper known locally as Ziggy has not been seen since being found with serious injuries consistent with a speargun attack near Mollymook, New South Wales. The fish is estimated to be over 30 years old and had been a familiar presence for snorkellers. Local conservation groups plan to seek warning signs; authorities have been contacted, and no suspect has been identified.

articles.title: BOJ's Tamura signals chance of faster-pace interest rate hikes
articles.summary: Bank of Japan board member Naoki Tamura said the central bank should move its policy rate toward a neutral level soon and could accelerate increases if inflation overshoots. He cited higher oil and raw-material costs, broadening wholesale price pressures, yen volatility and strong AI-related demand. Tamura said firms appear able to absorb past hikes, but his comments do not represent a board decision or guarantee a faster schedule.

articles.title: Brazil's Embraer CEO says US aircraft tariff will hurt airlines
articles.summary: Embraer CEO Francisco Gomes Neto said a proposed 10% U.S. tariff on finished Brazilian aircraft could raise airline costs and ticket prices. More than 40% of the E175's content is sourced from the United States, he told Reuters. The company expects no impact this year because any implementation would likely begin in 2027; the proposal remains subject to policy decisions.

articles.title: Brazil's Grupo Fictor, former bidder for Banco Master, investigated in fraud probe, source says
articles.summary: São Paulo police and prosecutors are investigating investment group Grupo Fictor over suspected fraud, money laundering and diversion of investor funds, Reuters reported. Authorities are executing 12 search warrants and courts are freezing 4.3 billion reais in assets. The state says more than 4 billion reais were raised through fixed-return promises unsupported by real operations; the company says it will cooperate.

articles.title: Brazil's Lula sounds out Bradesco chairman as finance minister, sources say
articles.summary: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has approached Bradesco chairman Luiz Carlos Trabuco about becoming finance minister, two sources told Reuters. Trabuco had not decided. The outreach follows market pressure and a weakening real after Lula's election win; investors reacted positively to reports of a market-friendly candidate. Lula is expected to announce an initial group of ministers next week, but no appointment has been confirmed.

articles.title: Britain signs £8 billion deal to upgrade submarine facilities
articles.summary: Britain signed a five-year, £8 billion contract with Babcock to upgrade nuclear-submarine maintenance facilities, aiming to reduce delays that have kept Royal Navy vessels on longer deployments. Defence officials cite a growing Russian threat and say the nuclear deterrent is a priority despite tight public finances. The programme is expected to create about 3,000 skilled jobs and 2,500 apprenticeship and graduate roles.

articles.title: Cameron Norrie gives Britain 1-0 lead over Germany in Davis Cup quarter-final
articles.summary: Cameron Norrie beat Germany's Jan-Lennard Struff 6-3, 3-6, 6-2 to give Britain a 1-0 lead in their Davis Cup quarter-final in Bologna. Norrie, ranked 52nd, recovered after losing the second set and finished in 93 minutes. Germany's Alexander Zverev was scheduled to face Arthur Fery next, with a doubles match to follow if needed; the winner advances to Saturday's semi-finals.

articles.title: China, Japan, South Korea and ASEAN launch talks on digital payments across borders
articles.summary: China, Japan, South Korea and ASEAN agreed to form a working group on connecting domestic payment systems and coordinating rules for digital assets across borders. Finance and central-bank officials met in Kyoto and also discussed an emergency lending mechanism that took effect this month for shocks such as natural disasters and pandemics. The initiative reflects rising demand for faster regional digital transactions.

articles.title: China's defence ministry urges Japan to stop 'stirring up' South China Sea disputes
articles.summary: China's defence ministry urged Japan to stop commenting on South China Sea disputes after Tokyo announced plans to provide the Philippines with coastal-surveillance radars and drones. Beijing says Japan is not a party to the disputes, while China and the Philippines regularly clash around contested reefs. China claims nearly the entire sea despite a 2016 tribunal ruling rejecting the legal basis of those claims.

articles.title: Crew member dies after diesel tanker sinks off Ibiza; Spain launches pollution plan
articles.summary: The Malta-flagged chemical tanker Med Emre sank about 25 nautical miles off Ibiza while carrying as much as 7,000 metric tons of diesel. All 17 crew members were rescued, but one later died and six were treated for minor injuries. Spain activated its second-highest maritime pollution response and sent specialist vessels to survey waters important to sea turtles, dolphins and seagrass; the cause and any spill remain unknown.

articles.title: Data centre rush drives biggest rise in Australian business investment since mining boom
articles.summary: Australian private capital spending rose 12.2% in the September quarter to A$59.5 billion, its biggest increase since 2011 and well above forecasts. Spending on information and telecommunications equipment jumped 87% as firms bought data-centre servers and processing gear, much of it imported. Businesses also raised planned investment for 2026–27, suggesting technology demand is resilient even as higher rates weigh on households.

articles.title: Data from Chinese AI firm MiniMax accessed by unidentified parties, researcher says
articles.summary: Cybersecurity researchers at Dragos said confidential links and other data submitted to Chinese AI firm MiniMax were accessed by unidentified parties, including after users requested that data not be retained. MiniMax said its systems automatically opened links to check for threats, deleted stored addresses and found no evidence chats or AI responses were disclosed. Atlas Cloud stopped forwarding requests and warned customers that secrets might be exposed.

articles.title: Deputy head of Polish central bank says probe of governor could damage economy
articles.summary: Deputy governor Marta Kightley warned that bringing Polish central-bank Governor Adam Glapinski before the State Tribunal could undermine central-bank independence and raise bond yields and debt costs. Lawmakers accuse him of unconstitutional asset purchases and politicising the bank; he rejects the claims. Parliament's vote date and the required threshold remain disputed after conflicting court rulings, leaving the proceeding's legality unresolved.

articles.title: Dollar rally takes a pause for Thanksgiving
articles.summary: The U.S. dollar paused near this year's highs as falling Treasury yields and a partial recovery in equities tempered demand for safe-haven assets ahead of Thanksgiving. Investors are weighing whether a slowdown in the AI trade could weaken U.S. growth and alter expectations for Federal Reserve policy. Thin holiday trading may amplify moves; the yen was near 159.19 per dollar and sterling slipped 0.2%.

articles.title: Dutch minister says US chip curbs bill would hurt Europe
articles.summary: Dutch Trade Minister Sjoerd Sjoerdsma called the proposed U.S. MATCH Act excessive, warning it could force allies such as the Netherlands and Japan to tighten China chip-equipment controls or face unilateral U.S. restrictions. The bill could hit ASML, which expects China to account for about 20% of this year's sales, and semiconductor firms across Europe. The Netherlands is working with the EU, Germany and France to block its inclusion in U.S. defence legislation.

articles.title: Ebola outbreak in Congo reaches 12,000 cases as violence forces some responders to evacuate
articles.summary: Congo’s Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak has reached 12,021 confirmed cases, with nearly half the patients dead, making it the country’s deadliest outbreak, AP reports. Fighting near Bunia has displaced residents, blocked health teams and reduced staffing at treatment centers; about a dozen people, including two WHO staff, were evacuated after being trapped in a hospital for three days. No approved vaccine or treatment exists for this strain.

articles.title: Egypt tanker explosion kills 31 people as driver crashes into fuel truck in fiery highway crash
articles.summary: Egyptian prosecutors say a driver was arrested after his car struck a fuel tanker on Cairo’s Ring Road, triggering a fire that killed 31 people and injured 21. The driver reportedly said he was changing lanes and travelling about 70 mph; at least 27 vehicles were destroyed. Authorities are investigating the crash, while the confirmed toll underscores persistent road-safety concerns.

articles.title: Emailed bomb threat against NT government ministers and public areas under investigation by NT Police
articles.summary: Northern Territory police are investigating an encrypted email threatening ministers, government staff and public places in Darwin. Police said specialist units were assessing the message and would treat it as credible until checks were complete; officials urged residents to remain alert but not alarmed. The sender's identity is unknown, and authorities have withheld specific targets while the investigation continues.

articles.title: Emirati curator Hoor Al Qasimi becomes first Arab woman to lead Venice Biennale art show
articles.summary: Emirati curator Hoor Al Qasimi was appointed to lead the 2028 Venice Biennale, becoming the first Arab and seventh woman to curate its main international art exhibition. She founded Sharjah Art Foundation and has led the Sharjah Biennial since 2003. Her role includes setting the exhibition's theme and selecting artists; the appointment follows controversy at the 2026 edition over Russia and Israel's participation.

articles.title: Explainer: Why are Indian rice prices rising despite record stocks?
articles.summary: Some rice varieties popular in southern India have nearly doubled in price over a year, pushing the national average up 12.5% in October despite record government stocks. Reuters attributes the squeeze to a weak monsoon, lower production and rising demand for broken rice from feed and ethanol makers. Large reserves are mostly common varieties that cannot readily replace preferred regional grades.

articles.title: FedEx airplane overruns runway at Miami airport, disrupting Thanksgiving travel
articles.summary: A FedEx MD-11 arriving from Memphis overran a runway at Miami International Airport around 8:40 p.m. Wednesday, temporarily closing all but one runway and causing hourslong delays into Thanksgiving morning. Authorities reported no injuries. The FAA is investigating, and FedEx said the aircraft experienced an issue on landing. The incident revived attention to runway safety after a separate fatal cargo-plane overrun at the airport in September.

articles.title: FIFA confirms cyberattack that accessed limited personal and business information
articles.summary: FIFA confirmed that a criminal cyberattack gave unauthorised access to a limited set of personal and business information. Reuters, citing a person with direct knowledge, reported that less than 0.1% of FIFA's data was affected and that files tied to the abandoned FIFA Forward Enterprise project were not accessed. FIFA did not disclose when the breach occurred, who was affected or whether stolen information was published.

articles.title: German consumer sentiment edges up into December, survey finds
articles.summary: Germany's consumer-climate index rose 0.7 points to -30.2 heading into December, but remained well below a healthy level and slightly missed analysts' expectations. Income expectations improved modestly, while economic expectations fell and price expectations increased. Researchers said the weak reading points to cautious Christmas spending, underscoring how persistent uncertainty and cost pressures continue to restrain household demand.

articles.title: German police arrest two Iraqis over alleged Cologne synagogue attack plot
articles.summary: German prosecutors said two Iraqi nationals were arrested after 17 raids in three states, suspected of belonging to a group that planned attacks on Jewish and other targets in Europe, including a Cologne synagogue. Investigators allege the group recruited operatives and raised funds for explosives; suspected members visited the synagogue and another European site in March, but no attack occurred. A judge was to decide whether the suspects remain in pretrial detention.

articles.title: Gold drifts lower as Fed rate-hike fears loom
articles.summary: Spot gold was down 0.4% at $3,565.41 an ounce by 0830 GMT after briefly falling below $3,500 the previous day, its first move under that level since September 2025. Reuters attributed pressure to persistent U.S. inflation and expectations of further Federal Reserve rate hikes. Higher rates make non-yielding bullion less attractive, though central-bank buying and future market shocks could support prices.

articles.title: Government gives environmental green light to Western Downs Digital Park
articles.summary: Australia's federal environmental regulator ruled that the proposed A$32 billion Western Downs Digital Park in Queensland does not need further federal assessment, finding it unlikely to significantly affect nationally protected matters. The project, backed by Anthropic, would be Australia's largest proposed data centre, but still needs state and local approvals. Critics warn its power demand could create major emissions if not supplied by renewables.

articles.title: Hong Kong marks deadly fire anniversary with flowers, prayers and tears
articles.summary: Hong Kong residents marked the first anniversary of the Wang Fuk Court fire, which killed 168 people, with flowers, prayers and memorials. The government had urged caution about commemorations it said could be exploited for disruption; rights groups and some survivors criticized the warning as chilling public mourning. Survivors remain displaced or in temporary housing, while questions about responsibility and fire-safety reforms remain unresolved.

articles.title: HSBC sees more than 100,000 users of its stablecoin in first month since launch
articles.summary: HSBC says more than 100,000 people used its Hong Kong dollar-backed RedCoin stablecoin during its first month. The token launched in October through the bank’s PayMe app, which has more than 3.3 million users, and can be transferred between people or spent at over 100,000 merchants. The bank says it will prioritize cybersecurity and additional products as usage expands.

articles.title: India asks Netflix not to air Pakistani show, local media report
articles.summary: India's government has asked Netflix not to stream a Pakistani series in the country, Reuters reported, following a complaint from a film-workers' union. The series, Netflix's first Urdu-language production, is scheduled for global release on December 4. Officials cited an earlier commitment not to offer Pakistan-originated content in India; Netflix had not responded to Reuters, and the reported request's legal status remains unclear.

articles.title: India orders tougher surveillance of packaged water, scrutiny set to cover PepsiCo, Coca-Cola
articles.summary: India’s food regulator ordered states to intensify inspections and risk-based sampling of packaged and mineral water after a Bisleri sample was flagged as unsafe. Reuters reports checks will also cover PepsiCo, Coca-Cola, Tata Consumer and Reliance Consumer in a market worth about $3.5 billion. Bisleri says its own testing found no problem; the regulator says it plans prosecution over alleged non-compliance.

articles.title: Indian farmers sell paddy stubble to biomass firms, reduce burning
articles.summary: Farmers in India's Punjab state are increasingly selling paddy straw to biomass plants instead of burning it, creating income and jobs while reducing a major source of seasonal air pollution. Farm fires fell 53% in 2025, but Delhi's air remained hazardous, showing the sector is still too small to change regional air quality. Analysts say procurement incentives and larger facilities are needed.

articles.title: Indonesian prosecutors name nickel firm and its owner as money laundering suspects
articles.summary: Indonesian prosecutors named nickel miner PT BSJ and its beneficial owner as suspects in an alleged money-laundering case tied to corruption in obtaining a mining permit from 2021 to 2026. Investigators say proceeds came partly from nickel ore sales under the licence. The owner could not be reached for comment, and the company did not respond to Reuters.

articles.title: Indonesian rescuers resume search for 13 people trapped inside illegal mine after 13 confirmed dead
articles.summary: Rescuers in West Java planned to resume searching for 13 workers trapped in an illegal gold mine after 13 of the 26 miners who entered Monday were confirmed dead. Heavy rain flooded the shaft about 100 metres underground. Six victims had been identified; narrow, slippery access and weather complicate the operation. Authorities say the site was unauthorized and unrelated to state miner Antam.

articles.title: Insight: Prosecco's 'heroic' vines offer a test case in climate resilience
articles.summary: Growers in Italy's Conegliano Valdobbiadene Prosecco region say the 2026 harvest held near last year's level despite record heat, drought and unusually warm nights. Reuters reports vineyards have adapted through less pruning, emergency irrigation and improved soil moisture, but these measures raise costs and may affect grape acidity. The experience offers a case study in climate adaptation, not proof the industry is insulated.

articles.title: Investors turn bullish on Indian rupee as Southeast Asian currency bets sour
articles.summary: A Reuters poll found investors bullish on the Indian rupee for the first time in 18 months, supported by more than $14 billion in November foreign-equity inflows and lower oil prices. The rupee recently reached an eight-month high, while bearish bets increased on the Indonesian rupiah, Thai baht and Philippine peso. Analysts caution the rupee's gains may be tactical as reserve rebuilding and a strong dollar could reverse the trend.

articles.title: Iran's Revolutionary Guards claim two tankers hit sea mines near Oman
articles.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said two tankers, including a supertanker carrying more than two million barrels, hit sea mines near Oman's Khasab while using an unauthorized Strait of Hormuz route; the claim has not been independently verified. Reuters reported oil prices rose as traders assessed shipping risks ahead of OPEC+'s November 29 meeting; sources said the group may keep first-quarter 2027 output targets unchanged.

articles.title: Iranian activist and Oscar-nominated screenwriter Mehdi Mahmoudian arrested in Tehran
articles.summary: Iranian rights activist and Oscar-nominated screenwriter Mehdi Mahmoudian was arrested at his Tehran home on Wednesday, a friend and activist told the Associated Press. Reports say agents seized his electronic devices; authorities had not publicly explained the detention. The arrest followed his warnings that two protesters jailed over the 2022 Mahsa Amini demonstrations faced imminent execution. He is reportedly held at Greater Tehran Penitentiary.

articles.title: Iraq court sentences eight French nationals to life for joining Islamic State
articles.summary: An Iraqi court sentenced eight French nationals to life in prison for joining the Islamic State group, AFP reported. Two other French defendants received 15-year terms, while verdicts for 10 more were postponed. The cases follow transfers of foreign detainees from Syria to Iraq, where authorities have been processing people accused of joining the group. The convictions and remaining proceedings may carry diplomatic and human-rights implications.

articles.title: Israel's Eisenkot reaches deal with left-wing faction as coalition talks gain steam
articles.summary: Gadi Eisenkot secured a coalition agreement with the left-wing Democrats faction, which would receive four ministerial posts, but he still lacks a majority. His bloc won 48 of 120 seats, while Benjamin Netanyahu's alliance has 53. A deal with Avigdor Lieberman's right-wing party could help, yet negotiations over ultra-Orthodox military conscription and other partners remain unresolved before the December 6 deadline.

articles.title: Israeli strikes kill 10 in Gaza, AP reports
articles.summary: AP's latest update said four Israeli strikes and a shooting killed 10 Palestinians across Gaza overnight and Thursday, including Hamas-appointed deputy education minister Khaled Abu Nada and his wife. Reuters separately reported at least nine deaths, reflecting different reporting windows. Israel said one strike targeted militants; near-daily fire continues despite the ceasefire, and casualty figures remain attributed to Gaza medical officials.

articles.title: Italy asks Germany to intervene over Henkel factory closure
articles.summary: Italy has asked Germany to intervene with Henkel over plans to close its Ferentino detergent plant by June 2027, a move affecting 102 workers. Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani wrote to his German counterpart seeking alternatives. Henkel has agreed not to begin formal dismissal procedures while talks continue; another meeting is scheduled in Rome for January 13.

articles.title: Japan property investment hits record as global funds target Tokyo and Osaka
articles.summary: Commercial property investment in Japan reached a quarterly record of 2.21 trillion yen ($13.9 billion) in the third quarter, up 4% year over year, while overseas purchases rose 30%, Reuters reported. Investors are targeting Tokyo and Osaka offices, hotels, logistics and data centres as rents rise and vacancies tighten. Higher interest rates, yen volatility and development costs are making leveraged core assets less attractive, so advisers favour selective, value-adding deals.

articles.title: Judge temporarily blocks FCC from early license review of ABC
articles.summary: A federal judge granted ABC a temporary restraining order and preliminary injunction blocking the FCC's early review of eight Disney-owned stations, finding the network likely to succeed on its First Amendment retaliation claim. The review followed President Trump's call for ABC to fire Jimmy Kimmel. The judge declined to bar unspecified future FCC actions; the agency says it will continue enforcing broadcasters' public-interest duties.

articles.title: Kenya cult leader found guilty of new assault and cruelty charges
articles.summary: Kenyan preacher Paul Mackenzie was found guilty of assault and cruelty to children in a new case linked to his Good News International Church. A court said six children were allegedly forced to fast and punished if they tried to eat or escape; 11 followers were charged and 24 people acquitted. Mackenzie, already serving 200 years for the deaths of 191 people, is due to be sentenced on the new charges December 17.

articles.title: Kenya government breached constitution in building US-backed Ebola quarantine site, court says
articles.summary: A Kenyan court ruled that the government breached constitutional provisions when constructing a U.S.-backed Ebola quarantine facility and ordered work to stop until conditions are met, including disclosure of the agreement with Washington. The ruling adds legal and transparency hurdles to a project intended for outbreak response; Reuters did not report when construction could resume.

articles.title: Kurtley Beale back in Wallabies gold for Ireland Test, Allan Alaalatoa to make 100th appearance
articles.summary: Kurtley Beale, 37, has been named on Australia's bench for its Nations Championship Test against Ireland, marking his first Wallabies selection since 2021. Coach Les Kiss said the veteran earned the place through performance and versatility, not as a farewell gesture. Allan Alaalatoa will earn his 100th cap and winger James Ramm is set for his international debut.

articles.title: Liberal senator Leah Blyth defects to One Nation in major blow for Angus Taylor
articles.summary: South Australian Liberal senator Leah Blyth defected to One Nation, becoming the party's first federal senator from the state and dealing a blow to opposition leader Angus Taylor. Blyth said she had lost confidence in the Liberals' ability to address immigration, spending and energy policy. Former colleagues accused her of self-interest; she said she had not discussed the move with them beforehand.

articles.title: London commuters braced for disruption as tube strike begins
articles.summary: London Underground drivers represented by the RMT began a 24-hour strike at noon Thursday in a dispute over a proposed four-day working week. The union says the plan threatens existing protections and could mean longer, less predictable shifts; Transport for London says the pattern is voluntary. Piccadilly and Circle lines were expected to be suspended, with wider disruption continuing into Friday.

articles.title: Major League Baseball sues players’ union ahead of lockout, trying to block possible antitrust suit
articles.summary: Major League Baseball and the owners of its 30 teams sued the players’ union and eight union leaders, seeking to block decertification and an antitrust challenge to a lockout. The current labor deal expires Dec. 1, and MLB says it expects a lockout if no agreement is reached. Owners want a salary cap, which players reject; the union called the lawsuit frivolous. A 2027 season disruption is possible.

articles.title: Malaysian air force facilities used to transport illicit drugs, minister says
articles.summary: Malaysia's interior minister said military aviation facilities were used in 21 transactions to move at least three metric tons of illicit drugs worth 156 million ringgit since August 2024. Seven air force personnel and six civilians were arrested as investigators pursue two criminal cells in Sabah. Authorities have not specified whether bases or aircraft were used; the inquiry is ongoing.

articles.title: Musk pledges two SpaceX shares for every U.S. child
articles.summary: Elon Musk says each U.S. child will receive two SpaceX shares—one from the company and one from him personally—an estimated $18 billion pledge covering roughly 72 million minors. Reuters reported the company share could transfer next month, while Musk's personal share would follow after his lockup expires in June 2027. The announcement came hours after the FCC approved SpaceX's plan for up to one million orbital data-centre satellites.

articles.title: NATO intern suspected of spying to remain in jail in Belgium after appeal
articles.summary: A Canadian intern at NATO's military headquarters near Mons will remain in pretrial detention while Belgian prosecutors appeal a court order that would have released her under electronic monitoring. She was arrested in July on suspicion of spying for a third country; sources told Reuters investigators suspect a China link. NATO says the case has not affected operations. The allegations remain unproven.

articles.title: Necessities join gifts in Black Friday shopping carts as AI and higher costs steer spending
articles.summary: U.S. shoppers are using extended Black Friday promotions to buy household basics alongside gifts, while AI tools help compare products and prices. Adobe Analytics said online spending reached $82.5 billion from Nov. 1–22, up 9.1% year over year, and forecast $275.1 billion for the holiday season. Retailers are spreading discounts across the month, blurring the traditional one-day kickoff.

articles.title: New Danish registry breach exposes personal data of 11,000 people
articles.summary: Hackers accessed personal information belonging to 11,000 people in Denmark's national civil registry, the government said. The breach came two months after an earlier attack exposed data linked to 8.8 million people. Officials said a new monitoring system detected and stopped the latest intrusion despite recent security upgrades. Authorities have not identified the attackers or disclosed the full scope of information accessed.

articles.title: No. 18 USC rallies, then holds on to edge South Carolina
articles.summary: No. 18 Southern California stayed unbeaten at 7–0 by rallying past South Carolina 71–69 in the Acrisure Series. Alijah Arenas scored 25 points, including 12 of 13 free throws, as USC closed on a 10–2 run and held the Gamecocks scoreless for the final 4:05. South Carolina led by as many as 10 but missed two late go-ahead shots.

articles.title: Norse Atlantic suspends flights, warns of possible bankruptcy
articles.summary: Norse Atlantic suspended flights and returned all aircraft to bases in Norway, Sweden and Britain as it seeks urgent financing. The board said it intends to file for bankruptcy if no short-term solution is secured; the company is also discussing a possible takeover but warned no viable solution is assured. Reuters reported fuel costs tied to the Iran war have erased about 99% of its market value this year.

articles.title: Nvidia halts server shipments to four Southeast Asian countries, FT reports
articles.summary: Reuters reported, citing the Financial Times, that Nvidia told manufacturing partners to stop shipping servers containing its chips to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia. The move follows new U.S. export-license requirements for advanced chips to several Southeast Asian countries, intended to block diversion to Chinese buyers. The report did not provide a detailed company statement explaining the halt.

articles.title: Nyk Lewis' late jumper lifts VCU past Washington in Maui
articles.summary: VCU beat Washington 80–78 in the Maui Invitational after Nyk Lewis hit a driving jumper with 1.8 seconds left. The Rams erased a 10-point second-half deficit with an 8–1 closing run; Washington’s Nikola Dzepina scored a career-high 31 points but missed a final long-range attempt. VCU improved to 5–2, while 17 Washington turnovers helped decide the game.

articles.title: Nyrstar to halt zinc production at Dutch smelter from November 30
articles.summary: Nyrstar, owned by Trafigura, will stop zinc production at its Budel smelter in the Netherlands from November 30, saying energy costs and weak market conditions make operations uneconomic. The site can produce 315,000 metric tons annually and had restarted in 2024 after an earlier shutdown. The company says it does not expect direct redundancies among permanent staff while its strategic review continues.

articles.title: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkey to meet on mutual defence pact
articles.summary: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkey will meet in Islamabad on November 27–28 to discuss their mutual-defence agreement, two Pakistani sources told Reuters. The Saudi and Turkish foreign ministers are expected to attend. The pact was signed in Mecca in August as regional tensions rose over the US-Israeli war with Iran. The meeting could deepen security coordination among three influential Muslim-majority states, but no new commitments were announced.

articles.title: Pakistan's first astronaut recites Iqbal poetry aboard China's Tiangong station
articles.summary: Pakistani astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali recited a couplet by national poet Muhammad Iqbal in Urdu aboard China's Tiangong space station, then translated its meaning into Mandarin for his Chinese crewmates. The moment echoed earlier references to Iqbal in space by Indian astronauts Rakesh Sharma and Kalpana Chawla. Ali is Pakistan's first astronaut and joined two Chinese crewmates on Shenzhou 24; the mission includes more than 90 experiments.

articles.title: Police use tear gas to disperse fresh Bangladesh garment worker protests
articles.summary: Bangladesh police used tear gas and sound grenades to disperse garment workers blocking a major highway, a day after a panel approved a 36% minimum-wage increase that protesters say is inadequate. A police motorcycle was set on fire in Gazipur, a major manufacturing hub; authorities said the situation later calmed. The industry employs millions and supplies much of the country's export earnings, making wage disputes economically significant.

articles.title: Portugal aims for 2027 surplus, PM refuses to enact deficit-driving tax cuts
articles.summary: Portugal's prime minister said he still expects a 2027 budget surplus after parliament-approved tax cuts pushed the official forecast to a 0.2% deficit. The measures, including a proposed temporary zero VAT rate on essential foods and capped fuel taxes, could cost about €800 million. Luis Montenegro said his government would not implement some provisions and may seek a Constitutional Court ruling, setting up a dispute over parliament's budget authority.

articles.title: Puerto Rico's Supreme Court cancels Luma power contract, leaving transition uncertain
articles.summary: Puerto Rico's Supreme Court voted 5–4 to cancel the government's contract with Luma Energy, allowing a one-year transition for officials to arrange a replacement. Outages remain a problem and the federal oversight board says there is no clear successor or transition plan. The ruling also prompted allegations of pressure on judges; members of the majority rejected them. Luma said it is reviewing legal options and warned of risks to grid modernization.

articles.title: Rare-earth recycler Cyclic Materials plans German plant and wider expansion
articles.summary: Cyclic Materials, backed by Microsoft, Amazon and BMW, has secured a site near Leipzig for a rare-earth magnet recycling plant planned to open in 2028. It expects the facility to process up to 25,000 metric tons of scrap annually and is planning four more European sites, with Asia expansion later. The company says recycling could help Western manufacturers reduce reliance on China, which processes about 90% of global rare earths.

articles.title: Rebel Estudiantes takes on rich Palmeiras for South America's biggest club prize
articles.summary: Palmeiras and Estudiantes meet Saturday in Montevideo for the Copa Libertadores title, with Palmeiras' squad valued at about $238 million—roughly four times Estudiantes'—after years of private investment and player sales. Estudiantes, a four-time champion returning to the final for the first time since 2009, is led by Juan Sebastián Verón, whose push for private capital has intensified a dispute with Argentina's football leadership.

articles.title: Russian court arrests deputy aerospace forces commander, Kommersant reports
articles.summary: Russian media outlet Kommersant reported that a military court arrested Yuriy Grekhov, deputy commander of Russia's Aerospace Forces and chief of armaments. Reuters said the arrest request came from the Military Investigative Committee, but the charge has not been disclosed. The force includes air, space and air-defence units, making the case notable amid scrutiny of Russia's military leadership.

articles.title: Russian oil refinery in Krasnodar region on fire after drone attack
articles.summary: A drone attack caused a fire at the Slavyansk ECO refinery in Russia's Krasnodar region, damaging a crude-distillation unit, storage facilities and pipelines, the company said. The site was already shut for maintenance after a September strike. Industry sources estimate attacks have cut Russian refinery processing volumes by 45% since late October; the current attack's perpetrators and repair timetable were not independently established.

articles.title: Rwanda raises benchmark rate to 9.5% as inflation reaches 19.5%
articles.summary: Rwanda's central bank raised its benchmark rate by 75 basis points to 9.5%, its fourth increase this year, as annual inflation reached 19.5% in October—far above the bank's 2–8% target band. It also lifted the reserve requirement for banks from 5% to 7%. Governor Soraya Hakuziyaremye expects inflation to ease toward the target from the second half of 2027, but cited weather risks to agricultural output.

articles.title: Serbia schedules presidential election for December 27 after student-led movement's win
articles.summary: Serbia will hold a presidential election on December 27, parliament speaker Aleksandar Cupic said, following an October parliamentary vote won by a student-led protest movement campaigning against corruption. Former president Aleksandar Vucic resigned in September to run for prime minister but lost the parliamentary contest. The presidency is largely ceremonial, while executive authority rests with the government and prime minister; the vote will shape the next stage of Serbia's political transition.

articles.title: Singapore 'very disappointed' over new tariffs, urges US to reconsider
articles.summary: Singapore's trade ministry rejected the U.S. Trade Representative's proposed maximum 20% tariff, which could fall to 10% if a reciprocal deal is reached, and said it would press Washington to reconsider. Officials argue the findings ignore Singapore's open, market-oriented economy and a U.S. trade surplus under their existing free-trade agreement. The dispute follows an eight-month U.S. investigation into alleged excess industrial capacity.

articles.title: Sinner to miss Australian Open after undergoing surgery on knee injury
articles.summary: Jannik Sinner will miss the Australian Open in January after surgery for a persistent knee injury, Tennis Australia confirmed. The world No. 2 has been sidelined since winning Wimbledon in July and had initially expected to return for Melbourne. Italian media reported he could be out for up to four months, but that longer estimate has not been confirmed by his team.

articles.title: South Korea unification minister nominee pledges 'realistic' approach to North Korea
