She says she is restoring trust and retains the support of Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.

articles.title: Chicago Cubs add LHP Trevor Rogers and Japanese slugger Teruaki Sato, AP source says
articles.summary: Chicago’s Cubs agreed to a five-year, $120 million contract with left-handed pitcher Trevor Rogers and a deal with Japanese slugger Teruaki Sato, according to an Associated Press source. Rogers adds a starter after a 10–11 season with Baltimore, while Sato arrives after winning Japan’s Central League Triple Crown and a second straight MVP. Both moves were pending physicals, and Sato’s strikeout rate is a question for MLB adjustment.

articles.title: China extends suspension of ban on US-bound gallium, germanium, antimony exports
articles.summary: China extended until Jan. 27, 2027, its suspension of restrictions on U.S.-bound exports of gallium, germanium, antimony and certain superhard materials, while keeping tighter end-use reviews for graphite. The pause had been due to expire Nov. 27. The minerals feed semiconductors, fiber optics, batteries and defense supply chains; the extension gives Washington and Beijing more time to maintain a fragile trade truce.

articles.title: China Southern orders 50 jets in Boeing's biggest China deal in nearly a decade
articles.summary: China Southern subsidiary Xiamen Airlines agreed to buy 50 Boeing 737 MAX 8 aircraft at a list price of about $7.4 billion, Reuters reports. Deliveries are scheduled for 2031–2034, making it the largest Chinese order for Boeing in nearly a decade. The purchase converts part of a 200-jet commitment announced at a U.S.-China summit, signaling a thaw in commercial aviation ties despite continuing trade tensions.

articles.title: China's Huawei convicted in sprawling US criminal trial over Iran business
articles.summary: A Brooklyn jury convicted Huawei on 10 of 12 federal counts, including bank fraud, wire fraud, sanctions violations and conspiracy to steal trade secrets, in a case stemming from the company’s Iran business and dealings with U.S. firms. Jurors rejected racketeering-conspiracy and obstruction counts. Huawei says it expects to appeal; sentencing is scheduled for September 2027, leaving penalties unresolved.

articles.title: Chinese researcher is in 'remarkable spirits' after ICE detention, professor says
articles.summary: Princeton neuroscience researcher Eva Yi Xie is being held in Virginia after immigration agents detained her at Reagan National Airport. Homeland Security says she overstayed her visa and lacked study authorization; her lawyer says a pending asylum application allows her to live and work in the U.S. A judge barred her removal from Virginia while reviewing a challenge to the detention, and Princeton colleagues are seeking answers.

articles.title: Climate scientists urge US lawmakers to vote no on sweeping permitting bill
articles.summary: More than 120 climate scientists urged the U.S. House to reject the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, arguing that its permitting changes could lock in fossil-fuel projects and weaken environmental safeguards. Supporters say the bill would speed clean-energy and transmission construction and reduce electricity costs. The Senate has passed it, and House lawmakers are considering amendments before a vote; the legislation’s effects remain contested.

articles.title: College Football Playoff rankings put Georgia, Utah, Texas and Notre Dame in top four
articles.summary: The fourth College Football Playoff rankings placed Georgia, Utah, Texas and Notre Dame in the top four, with Tennessee rising from ninth to fifth after other contenders stumbled. Alabama fell to sixth and UCLA to ninth, while Wake Forest moved into the top ten. The committee’s list shapes the final selection race, with two more rankings releases scheduled before the playoff field is set.

articles.title: Daniels leads winning drive as Commanders walk off Bengals in thriller
articles.summary: Washington beat Cincinnati 22–20 after quarterback Jayden Daniels led a 64-yard drive in the final 34 seconds, setting up Drew Stevens’ 26-yard field goal as time expired. Daniels connected twice with rookie Antonio Williams after the Bengals had taken a one-point lead. The win kept Washington in the NFC East race and ended Cincinnati’s five-game winning streak. The Associated Press noted Washington’s six consecutive scoring drives of more than 50 yards.

articles.title: Democrat Victoria Broderick unseats eight-term Republican incumbent in Tennessee to win election
articles.summary: Democrat Victoria Broderick won Tennessee's 4th congressional district, defeating eight-term Republican Scott DesJarlais by fewer than 400 votes after a redrawn map made the seat slightly more competitive. The upset lifts Democrats' House majority to 259, their largest in three decades, and makes Broderick the only Democrat in Tennessee's congressional delegation. The race had been rated safely Republican.

articles.title: Democrats aim to reverse Trump's slashes to US food aid, but path unclear
articles.summary: Democratic leaders say they will seek to reverse $187 billion in food-assistance cuts when they take control of Congress in January. Reuters reports more than 5.5 million people have lost Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program benefits since the 2025 tax law, while food banks report sustained demand. Democrats have not settled on a legislative route, and a veto threat means overriding the president would require broad Republican support.

articles.title: Dozens of oil and shipping tankers hacked in recent weeks, per report
articles.summary: TechCrunch reported, citing The Wall Street Journal, that U.S. officials suspect Iranian hackers may be behind as many as 50 recent cyberattacks on oil and shipping vessels. The targeted ships carried oil, liquefied gas and other hazardous cargo across Asia and Europe; earlier navigation-system breaches also prompted FBI and Coast Guard teams to board tankers near the U.S. The allegations have not been independently confirmed publicly.

articles.title: Draft Smithsonian overhaul plan prompts questions about White House influence
articles.summary: A Washington Post investigation reports that a photographed draft plan titled “Smithsonian Institution Renewal Plan” proposed sweeping changes to museum leadership, exhibitions, grants and internal policies. The document surfaced after a commuter photographed a White House aide working on it aboard the D.C. Metro. A Democratic lawmaker pledged oversight hearings, while Smithsonian leaders defended the institution’s independence and said the plan’s intended use was unclear.

articles.title: Elon Musk asks appeals court to overturn Twitter shareholder fraud verdict
articles.summary: Elon Musk asked a U.S. appeals court to overturn a jury verdict that found he defrauded Twitter shareholders by publicly questioning his 2022 takeover agreement. His lawyers argue investors did not prove his posts caused the stock decline and challenge the class-action certification. Reuters says the shareholders’ lawyers estimate damages could reach $2.6 billion plus interest if the verdict stands; the appeal remains unresolved.

articles.title: Even the best AI agents struggle with everyday life
articles.summary: A new ShellBench benchmark suggests that even leading AI models from OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta struggle with everyday tasks that require reliable judgment. The systems failed more than one-third of attempts, while 15.7% of all tested attempts violated at least one safety requirement, sometimes causing unintended consequences. The findings challenge claims that consumer agents are ready to manage shopping, travel and other personal responsibilities autonomously.

articles.title: Experts debunk Thanksgiving food myths, from turkey ‘coma’ to risky leftovers
articles.summary: AP’s Thanksgiving guide says the 1621 meal is poorly documented: the surviving account mentions deer and fowl but not turkey specifically, and likely omitted potatoes and sweetened cranberry sauce. Nutrition experts say turkey’s tryptophan does not cause the familiar post-meal “coma”; large carbohydrate-heavy meals contribute more. Leftovers should be refrigerated within two hours and eaten within three to four days.

articles.title: FHFA raises 2027 conforming loan limit to $855,400 for most U.S. homes
articles.summary: The Federal Housing Finance Agency will let Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac buy or guarantee single-family mortgages up to $855,400 in most U.S. counties beginning in 2027, a 2.7% increase. Higher limits apply in expensive areas, including $1.28 million in Los Angeles County and $1.22 million in New York County. The change reflects rising home values, while elevated mortgage rates continue to weigh on sales.

articles.title: Five Turkish soldiers killed in helicopter crash, ministry says
articles.summary: Turkey’s Defence Ministry said five soldiers died when an AS-532 military helicopter crashed during a training flight in central Eskişehir province. The ministry did not disclose a cause, and Reuters reported no immediate details about weather, mechanical issues or an investigation. The incident adds to military aviation losses that can involve complex training and maintenance factors, but the available information does not establish what brought the aircraft down.

articles.title: French officials order former President Sarkozy's corruption case to trial
articles.summary: French authorities have sent a case involving former President Nicolas Sarkozy and his wife, Carla Bruni, to trial over alleged efforts to secure the retraction of testimony linking Sarkozy’s 2007 campaign to Libyan money. The witness, businessman Ziad Takieddine, later withdrew his account and has since died. Sarkozy and Bruni deny wrongdoing; the case is separate from his earlier Libya-financing conviction, which he is appealing. A pre-trial hearing is set for April 2027.

articles.title: Gavi plans to buy up to 1.5 million doses of experimental Ebola vaccine for Congo
articles.summary: Gavi plans to buy up to 1.5 million doses of an experimental vaccine against the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola if trials in the Democratic Republic of Congo show it is safe and effective. The candidate was developed by Oxford and the Serum Institute of India. No licensed vaccine or treatment exists for this strain, which has caused a major outbreak; purchase terms were not disclosed.

articles.title: Gaza issues meningitis epidemic alert after infections surge
articles.summary: Gaza's health ministry reported 272 meningitis infections in October, more than eight times the usual monthly range, and issued an epidemic alert. Fifteen people have died since the start of 2026, according to the ministry. Aid agencies cite overcrowded shelters, sewage-contaminated water, damaged infrastructure and restricted supplies as contributing conditions. The figures include suspected cases, and independent verification is difficult amid the continuing humanitarian emergency.

articles.title: Gisèle Pelicot condemns publisher over use of intimate images in book promotion
articles.summary: Gisèle Pelicot criticized a Paris publisher for using intimate photographs taken by her former husband to promote a book about her rape case. Her lawyer said the images were part of evidence in the trial that convicted 51 men, including her ex-husband. The publisher apologized, halted promotion and said it would not print more copies, while disputing descriptions of the images as explicit.

articles.title: GTA VI PC recompilation project shut down by Take-Two
articles.summary: Take-Two used a DMCA notice to remove Leonida, a fan project translating a leaked Xbox build of Grand Theft Auto VI into native Windows code, along with more than 2,900 forks. The Verge reports modders continue trying other recompilation and compatibility projects, but rebuilding the full game remains difficult. The dispute highlights the publisher’s copyright enforcement as unofficial PC efforts accelerate.

articles.title: Holiday shoppers return to malls for in-person experiences
articles.summary: Retail surveys indicate renewed interest in physical shopping ahead of Thanksgiving. A JLL survey found approximately 55% of holiday shoppers intended to visit an indoor mall, compared with around half last year. Retailers are adding dining, customization and other experiences to attract visitors. The figures reflect shoppers' stated plans rather than final holiday sales.

articles.title: House Democrat expands investigation into Donald Trump Jr.'s investment firm
articles.summary: House Judiciary Democrat Jamie Raskin requested two years of records from four companies linked to Donald Trump Jr.’s investment firm 1789 Capital, saying he is examining whether investments preceded favorable federal contracts or policy decisions. Trump Jr. and the firm deny wrongdoing, and companies gave varied responses. The inquiry could become a major oversight issue when Democrats take control of the House in January.

articles.title: Hungary, Ukraine make 'fresh start' as Magyar visit kickstarts trade talks
articles.summary: Hungarian Prime Minister Peter Magyar and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy called their meeting a fresh start and discussed trade, energy and rail links. Hungary had blocked parts of Ukraine’s EU accession process under former leader Viktor Orban; Magyar has eased some objections after Kyiv expanded language rights for minorities. No major deals were announced, but the visit signals warmer ties after years of friction.

articles.title: Iranian singer and four colleagues receive lashes, prompting criticism
articles.summary: Iranian singer Parastoo Ahmadi and four members of her concert team each received 74 lashes in Qom, their lawyer told Iran International, after an online performance filmed without a live audience. The punishment prompted criticism from artists and activists and renewed scrutiny of restrictions on women singing publicly and compulsory-hijab rules. An appeals court had upheld their sentences in September, including bans on artistic activity and foreign travel.

articles.title: Israeli airstrike kills senior Hamas security official in Gaza
articles.summary: An Israeli airstrike killed Naeem Abu Nahel, whom Palestinian officials identified as the head of Hamas’ internal security apparatus in Gaza, Reuters reports. Medics said at least six other Palestinians were killed in separate strikes, including police officers. Israel said it targeted militants; Hamas denied efforts to rearm and accused Israel of undermining the ceasefire. The attacks underscore that the 2025 truce has not ended violence in Gaza.

articles.title: Istanbul authorities reverse course on reported lioness
articles.summary: Authorities launched a day-long search after videos appeared to show a lioness in an Istanbul suburb. Residents were advised to remain indoors and a forest was closed. Officials subsequently said further images and field searches produced no evidence of a lion or other large feline. The animal’s actual identity remained unclear, prompting public confusion and jokes online.

articles.title: Japan looks to auto-parts suppliers to expand its defense industry
articles.summary: Japan is encouraging automotive component manufacturers to diversify into defense production as part of a broader security buildup. Reuters reports that procurement officials are connecting smaller suppliers with defense companies and funding opportunities. The initiative could create new markets for an auto industry facing declining domestic production. Major Japanese automakers have so far shown less interest than smaller suppliers.

articles.title: Justice Department announces largest-ever crackdown on scammers, targeting over 800 defendants
articles.summary: The Justice Department said it had taken action in more than 400 cases involving over 800 defendants since a March executive order targeting scam networks. The department cited charges, extraditions, convictions and international raids; the FBI said Operation Blackout seized nearly $17 billion in illicit funds and prevented more than $690 million in potential losses. Those figures are the administration's reported enforcement results, not an independent estimate of recovered victim money.

articles.title: Libya's Tripoli government asks court to annul disputed Arkenu oil deal
articles.summary: Libya’s internationally recognised Tripoli government has asked a court to suspend and annul a production-sharing agreement with Arkenu Oil Company covering two major fields. A U.N. expert panel previously said the company moved more than $3 billion abroad; Arkenu disputes that characterization and says it operated under a valid state-backed contract. The dispute reflects continuing tensions over control and transparency in Libya’s oil sector.

articles.title: Life expectancy in Cuba falls for first time since 1950 amid economic crisis
articles.summary: World Health Organization chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said Cuba’s life expectancy fell from 78.8 years in 2020 to 74.4 in 2025, the first decline since records began in 1950. He also cited worsening infant and maternal mortality and lower childhood-cancer survival. The figures predate a U.S. fuel blockade imposed in January; the WHO chief pointed to both external sanctions and domestic economic problems.

articles.title: Major law firms recruit teams after Weil's dissolution
articles.summary: The dissolution of Weil, Gotshal & Manges has prompted intense competition for its approximately 1,200 attorneys. Reuters documents groups moving to firms including Gibson Dunn, Skadden and Kirkland & Ellis, with hiring spanning private funds, restructuring and litigation. Milbank is taking on the Paris team. The moves illustrate how the collapse is reshaping the market for legal talent.

articles.title: Martha Ford, former Lions owner with link to auto giants, dies at 101
articles.summary: Martha Firestone Ford, former principal owner of the Detroit Lions and a member of the Firestone and Ford families, has died at 101. She took control of the NFL team after her husband’s death in 2014 and led it until 2020, when her daughter succeeded her. Ford remained involved in Detroit civic and health organizations and attended Lions games into her final year.

articles.title: Meta launches Muse in UK – the AI agent that can do your Christmas shopping
articles.summary: Meta launched its Muse AI assistant in the UK, where users can connect selected apps and ask it to shop, book travel, manage calendars or draft messages. Meta says the agent cannot purchase items or send messages without approval and has no access to passwords or payment details. UK privacy and competition regulators are monitoring the rollout after reports of testing errors, including incorrect reminders and financial information.

articles.title: Mexico reports 12 active measles cases as vaccination coverage reaches 90%
articles.summary: Mexico reported 12 active measles cases, all in Chiapas, while its health minister said about 90% of the population was vaccinated and ten million doses were available. The Pan American Health Organization says sustained transmission has cost Mexico its measles-free status and that at least 95% two-dose coverage is needed to stop transmission. The country must show 12 months without spread to regain certification.

articles.title: Michigan drops plans to hire new AD Trev Alberts, faces $21 million payout
articles.summary: Michigan abandoned plans to hire Texas A&M athletic director Trev Alberts, potentially triggering more than $21 million in payments and a legal dispute. Alberts had signed a five-year agreement worth $3.2 million annually plus bonuses; the university cited an unacceptable background check. The decision adds to instability in Michigan’s athletic department as it seeks new leadership for its football program.

articles.title: More than 300 Russians killed as Moscow props up Mali’s junta, leaked data reveals
articles.summary: Leaked Russian state death records reviewed by the Guardian list 349 Russian fighters killed in Mali between September 2023 and September 2026, including 43 deaths on the day insurgents attacked Kidal in April. Western officials said the toll exceeded earlier estimates, though the records may be incomplete. The figures illuminate the human cost of Moscow’s support for Mali’s military government as insecurity has continued despite Russia’s growing role.

articles.title: Myanmar earthquake reveals how fault history could help anticipate future slip
articles.summary: Researchers used hundreds of supercomputer simulations and data from GPS, satellites, seismometers and video to study the magnitude 7.8 Myanmar earthquake in 2025. The models suggest that a fault’s history can help estimate likely slip patterns and rupture speed before a future quake. Scientists stress this is not precise earthquake prediction; the work aims to improve hazard assessment and rapid response.

articles.title: Nearly 7,000 killed or injured by landmines, war remnants in 2025, highest toll in 5 years
articles.summary: The Landmine Monitor 2026 report recorded at least 6,929 people killed or injured by mines and explosive remnants in 2025, a 10% rise and the highest toll since 2020. Civilians accounted for 84% of known casualties, with children half of civilian victims whose ages were recorded. Myanmar had the most casualties; treaty withdrawals and renewed mine production are putting the international ban under pressure.

articles.title: New workflow advances programmable chromosome editing in plants
articles.summary: A team at the Chinese Academy of Sciences published a protocol for programmable, large-scale chromosome editing in plants, enabling insertions, deletions, inversions and replacements across substantial DNA regions. The method combines engineered recombinases with prime editing and aims to remove leftover editing sequences. Researchers say the workflow could support crop breeding and synthetic biology, though edited plant lines still require validation and take months to produce.

articles.title: Pope Francis' private diary reveals spiritual doubts and a period of crisis
articles.summary: The Vatican released excerpts from Pope Francis’ private diary, spanning 1992 to August 2024, revealing spiritual doubts, health struggles and reflections on the clergy-abuse scandal. The notes describe a 2021–22 crisis that a close aide linked to Francis’ struggles with authority and governance. The book was curated by Cardinal Víctor Manuel Fernández, who says Francis wanted the writings published.

articles.title: Radar outage delays arrivals at Chicago O'Hare during Thanksgiving travel
articles.summary: A ground-surveillance radar outage at Chicago O’Hare delayed arrivals during one of the busiest Thanksgiving travel days, the FAA said. The agency warned that congestion could force another temporary halt to incoming flights; average delays reached 47 minutes, with some aircraft holding before landing. The incident added to a series of aviation technology disruptions, though officials expected technicians to restore the system overnight.

articles.title: Reported cyber breach affects unclassified U.S. intelligence data
articles.summary: A person familiar with the incident told Reuters that the CIA and the Office of the Director of National Intelligence discovered unauthorized access to unclassified information. The affected network analyzes publicly available material. Officials said classified systems and essential capabilities had not been disrupted. The information exposed and the means of intrusion were not established in the report.

articles.title: Rope bridges help protect sloths from habitat loss in Costa Rica
articles.summary: Conservationists in Costa Rica have installed about 410 rope bridges to help sloths cross gaps in forest canopies fragmented by roads, hotels and development. The bridges reduce the need for the slow-moving animals to descend to the ground, where vehicles, dogs and power lines pose risks. Researchers say crossings and habitat corridors help, but long-term survival still depends on protecting and reconnecting forests.

articles.title: Sanofi's $41 billion Insmed bet charts life beyond Dupixent
articles.summary: Sanofi agreed to acquire U.S. respiratory-drug maker Insmed for $41 billion in cash, offering $175 a share, a 17.5% premium to the prior close. The deal would add marketed medicines and a respiratory pipeline as Sanofi seeks growth beyond Dupixent ahead of patent expiries in the early 2030s. Closing is expected in the first half of 2027, subject to approvals; analysts say it does not resolve every pipeline risk.

articles.title: Santas and a polar bear emerge from washed-up container on Bulgarian beach
articles.summary: Bulgarian authorities found life-size Santa figures, a polar-bear statue and holiday decorations inside a shipping container washed ashore near Burgas. Officials suspect it may have come from the Greek cargo ship Contship Jet, which sank after a drone strike in October, but the vessel’s operator could not confirm the link. The container’s arrival highlights wider maritime-security concerns in the Black Sea as Russia’s war continues.

articles.title: Senegal reinstated as 2025 African champions, Morocco to contest decision
articles.summary: Senegal was reinstated as 2025 Africa Cup of Nations champion after the Court of Arbitration for Sport unanimously overturned CAF’s decision to award Morocco a 3-0 forfeit. CAS restored Senegal’s 1-0 extra-time win, saying the referee’s choice to resume the final after the team’s walk-off was a field-of-play decision. Morocco said it would challenge the ruling; Senegal and the arbitrator denied alleged improper contact.

articles.title: Shein agrees to $100 million FTC settlement over shipping and review practices
articles.summary: Shein agreed to pay $100 million to settle U.S. Federal Trade Commission claims involving misleading shipping promises, filtered negative reviews and unsupported statements about cotton sourcing and supplier audits. The company did not admit liability and said it disagreed with some allegations. Reuters reports the settlement also requires changes to consumer practices, while the FTC says funds will be used to reimburse customers.

articles.title: South African court convicts man over plans to fight for Russia
articles.summary: A Zimbabwean man pleaded guilty in South Africa to violating legislation regulating foreign military assistance after agreeing to fight for Russia in Ukraine in exchange for payment. He received a suspended five-year sentence and faces deportation. The case comes amid wider concerns in several African countries about recruitment for the war and the treatment of recruits.

articles.title: South Korea issues alert after Russian warplanes enter air-defense zone near eastern island
articles.summary: Several Russian warplanes entered South Korea's air-defense identification zone near Ulleung Island, prompting Seoul to issue a brief public alert and summon Russia's military attaché. South Korea said the aircraft approached its territorial airspace but did not cross it; the alert was lifted after three minutes. Moscow said its aircraft acted within international law and disputes the legal basis of the zone. The incident followed other recent Russian aircraft entries.

articles.title: Spain extends bank tax and proposes tougher rules for consumer lending
articles.summary: Spain’s government extended its bank levy for another year, expecting about €1.4 billion for social housing and support for vulnerable tenants, and proposed new caps on some high-cost consumer loans. Consumer lending has reached a record €117.8 billion. Both measures still need parliamentary approval; banks have challenged the tax, and a possible conservative-led government after Sunday’s election could weaken or repeal it.

articles.title: Spanish government challenges Madrid regional law extending rights to unborn children
articles.summary: Spain’s Socialist-led government said it will challenge a Madrid regional law that makes unborn children eligible for certain family benefits, including tax breaks and subsidies. Equality Minister Ana Redondo argues the measure conflicts with national law and could affect abortion rights; the regional government is led by the conservative People’s Party. The dispute is entering a national election campaign, while Madrid’s law remains regional and the Constitutional Court has yet to rule.

articles.title: States sue HUD over rule that could end housing aid for mixed-status families
articles.summary: Twenty-one states and Pennsylvania’s governor sued HUD over a rule taking effect Dec. 14 that would end federal housing aid for an entire mixed-status household if any member lacks eligible immigration status. States say the change could displace U.S.-citizen children and families that previously received prorated assistance. HUD argues the rule enforces eligibility law and redirects limited funds; the court challenge will test that interpretation.

articles.title: Study compares AI's water use with almond milk and golf spending
articles.summary: An Enverus study reported by Reuters compares water use per dollar spent across activities, estimating that $25 of AI services consumes about 1.9 gallons, including water used to generate electricity. The report puts the same spending on almond milk at 308 gallons and golf at 679. The comparison depends on the study’s spending-based method and does not mean data centers have no local water impacts.

articles.title: Swedish parliament to vote on Moderates leader Kristersson to remain prime minister
articles.summary: Sweden’s parliament speaker nominated Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson for a November 30 confirmation vote, seeking to end a 72-day impasse after September’s election. His centre-right bloc lacks a majority, while centre-left parties have been unable to agree on a governing arrangement. The pivotal Centre Party has not chosen a side and rejects cooperation with both the Left Party and Sweden Democrats, leaving a fresh election possible if parliament cannot approve a prime minister.

articles.title: The New York Times warns photographers not to update Photoshop over AI features
articles.summary: The New York Times has told freelance photographers not to use Adobe Photoshop 2027 on Times assignments, warning that newer AI tools may add metadata identifying images as AI-generated or edited. The Verge reports the policy is intended to protect the paper’s rules against retouching and digital manipulation. The Times has not specified which features trigger the tags, and Adobe had not responded.

articles.title: The saguaro cactus, icon of the American West, struggles to survive
articles.summary: Reuters' investigation describes how hotter nights and prolonged heat waves are threatening Arizona's saguaro cactus, a species adapted to desert extremes but dependent on cool nighttime recovery. The cactus can live for more than 150 years and grow over 40 feet, yet researchers in Phoenix have attributed rising mortality to heat. Conservationists warn the iconic plant faces mounting stress as the Sonoran Desert warms.

articles.title: Thousands of Sikh pilgrims from India celebrate Guru Nanak’s 557th birthday in Pakistan
articles.summary: More than 5,000 worshippers gathered in Nankana Sahib, Pakistan, to mark the 557th birthday of Guru Nanak, Sikhism’s founder; officials said Pakistan issued more than 3,000 visas to Indian pilgrims. The gathering brought devotees from neighboring India to a major Sikh shrine despite strained India-Pakistan relations. Pilgrims are also scheduled to visit other sacred sites before returning home.

articles.title: Threads comes to iPad and adds cashtags for stock discussions
articles.summary: Meta has released an iPad version of Threads and added cashtags, which let users follow discussions tied to publicly traded companies. The tablet layout gives the social network more room for simultaneous conversations, while the stock tags borrow a feature popularized by X. The additions broaden Threads’ appeal beyond short text posts as Meta competes for users and financial discussion.

articles.title: Tidal bans 100% AI-generated music with plans to delete more than 27m tracks
articles.summary: Tidal says it will remove music it determines to be entirely AI-generated beginning December 9, a policy that could affect about 27 million tracks. The company said 43% of uploads in the previous 90 days were fully AI-generated and most received no streams. AI-assisted recordings remain eligible. The move is stricter than policies at Spotify and Apple Music and raises questions about how platforms will verify authorship.

articles.title: Tidal will start banning AI-generated music next month
articles.summary: Tidal says it will begin removing wholly AI-generated music on Dec. 9 and reject future submissions made entirely by AI tools. The Verge reports the company estimates 43% of tracks distributed to it over the prior 90 days were fully AI-generated, while 96% received no plays. AI-assisted work remains allowed when AI is not the sole source of the finished track.

articles.title: Trump grants Thanksgiving pardons for turkeys Freedom and Feathers at the White House
articles.summary: President Donald Trump pardoned two West Virginia turkeys, Freedom and Feathers, at the White House's annual Thanksgiving ceremony. Only Freedom attended in person after an online public vote; both birds will retire at Texas A&M University. Trump mixed holiday remarks with political comments about Democrats' midterm victories. The modern annual presidential tradition dates to George H.W. Bush's administration in 1989.

articles.title: Trump nominates North Carolina prosecutor who lost re-election for federal judgeship
articles.summary: President Donald Trump nominated Jim O’Neill, a North Carolina district attorney who lost his November re-election bid, for a lifetime federal judgeship. The nomination is part of a push to confirm judicial candidates before Democrats take control of the Senate on January 3. O’Neill has served as Forsyth County district attorney since 2009; nineteen other nominees remain pending, according to Reuters.

articles.title: U2's new album is about 'defiant joy.' They'll tour it in North America next summer
articles.summary: U2 announced a 15-date North American stadium tour for 2027 following the release of its first album of new songs in nine years, “Carnaval de Luz.” The run begins in Miami in August and ends in Vancouver in October, with presales starting Nov. 30 and general sales Dec. 4. The band says the album and show emphasize collective celebration; drummer Larry Mullen Jr. has returned after surgery.

articles.title: Uber and Nuro begin driverless testing of Lucid robotaxis ahead of 2027 launch
articles.summary: Uber and autonomous-vehicle startup Nuro have begun testing driverless Lucid Gravity SUVs on public streets in the San Francisco Bay Area. The companies say employee rides will follow as they prepare a commercial robotaxi launch in the first quarter of 2027. The tests mark a step toward removing human safety drivers, but regulatory approvals, operational performance and public acceptance remain key hurdles.

articles.title: UK warns AI-driven cyberattacks are exposing years of weak security
articles.summary: The U.K. government’s cybersecurity unit says AI-assisted attacks have risen markedly, with hackers using autonomous tools to identify and exploit basic weaknesses in networks. Officials warn the technology can speed up intrusion attempts and expose long-standing security gaps, rather than relying only on novel vulnerabilities. The warning puts pressure on organizations to improve patching and basic defenses as AI-enabled tools become more accessible.

articles.title: UK warns of Russian sabotage threat to companies that supply Ukraine
articles.summary: Britain’s Ministry of Defence and MI5 warned companies supplying Ukraine’s military that they face heightened sabotage risks from Russian-linked operatives. The public alert cites arson and other low-tech tactics and follows suspected incidents across Europe. Russia denies plans to attack the United Kingdom and accuses Ukraine of staging sabotage. British officials are briefing defense and infrastructure firms on security precautions.

articles.title: UN estimates five women or girls killed each hour by partners or relatives in 2025
articles.summary: UN Women and the UN Office on Drugs and Crime estimate that intimate partners or family members killed 47,000 women and girls worldwide in 2025—about five every hour and 60% of all 78,000 intentional killings of women and girls. Africa had the highest rate. The agencies caution that the lower estimate than 2024 reflects improved data availability, not a real decline; recorded cases likely understate the toll.

articles.title: UN warns HIV infections could rise again as global funding falls
articles.summary: UNAIDS chief Winnie Byanyima warned that new HIV infections could begin rising in 2027 as international funding cuts and prevention-service closures threaten recent progress. New infections fell to 1.2 million last year, a record low, despite global HIV funding dropping nearly one-fifth. The warning is a forecast based on emerging signs; full data confirming a reversal are not yet available.

articles.title: Underwater robots reveal first salp species known to live exclusively in deep sea
articles.summary: Researchers using remotely operated underwater vehicles have formally described Vitreosalpa gemini, a glass salp found only in deep ocean waters. The gelatinous animal lives roughly 280 to 2,200 meters below the surface, where it feeds on detritus and tiny organisms rather than surface phytoplankton. Its unusual reproductive cycle and role in moving carbon to the seafloor add to evidence that deep-sea ecosystems remain poorly documented.

articles.title: US consumer confidence jumps to highest level in nearly two years
articles.summary: U.S. consumer confidence rose to 103.3 in November from 91.9 in October, its second consecutive monthly gain. Respondents grew more optimistic about job availability as gasoline fell to an average $3.61 a gallon, down 17 cents in a week. Confidence improved most among Democrats and independents but slipped among Republicans; inflation remains a concern, and surveys may not reliably predict actual spending.

articles.title: US farm secretary pledges to fight court order halting her religious emails
articles.summary: U.S. Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins said she will appeal a federal judge’s ruling limiting religious messages sent to USDA staff through her official account. Employees and their union argued that agency-wide Christmas and Easter emails promoted Christianity in a way that could pressure workers. The judge said Rollins must respect boundaries, including stopping such messages when asked. Rollins says she will fight the decision through the Supreme Court.

articles.title: US lawmakers question FAA rollout of AI-assisted air traffic planning tool
articles.summary: Two dozen House Democrats questioned the Federal Aviation Administration’s nationwide rollout of SMART, an AI-assisted air-traffic planning tool, after a major telecom outage disrupted flights. The system analyzes schedules, weather and airport capacity to flag potential conflicts, but does not control aircraft. Lawmakers say they have not seen enough validation or redundancy evidence; the FAA said it would respond directly to their questions.

articles.title: US to host Copa America for second successive tournament in 2028
articles.summary: CONMEBOL and CONCACAF said the United States will host the 2028 Copa América from June 9 to July 9, with 10 South American teams joined by six from North America, Central America and the Caribbean. The six CONCACAF entrants will qualify through the 2027 Gold Cup. It will be the U.S. third time hosting and second consecutive edition; host cities and venues have not yet been announced.

articles.title: Walmart teams up with Meta to bring Black Friday deals to AI agent Muse
articles.summary: Walmart is partnering with Meta to let shoppers use the Muse AI agent to find, compare and purchase Black Friday deals. Customers can describe what they want instead of navigating Walmart’s site directly, giving the retailer a new route into AI-assisted commerce. The move contrasts with Amazon’s efforts to restrict third-party agents from completing purchases, highlighting competing strategies for agent-based shopping.

articles.title: Wendy’s hit with US class action over menu pricing
articles.summary: A proposed U.S. class action accuses Wendy’s and restaurant-software provider NCR Voyix of using shared transaction data and centralized pricing to coordinate menu prices across franchises. The complaint was filed in Maryland and has not been proven in court. The companies had not responded to Reuters’ requests for comment at publication. The case adds to litigation challenging how retailers use algorithmic pricing tools and sales data.

articles.title: What it’s like inside Rikers Island as jail staff prepare for Thanksgiving
articles.summary: Rikers Island staff prepared about 10,000 Thanksgiving lunches, using more than 6,000 pounds of turkey for inmates and employees. Each incarcerated person was due four ounces with traditional sides and dietary alternatives. The jail houses about 6,700 people and remains plagued by violence and overcrowding; New York’s mayor has proposed closing it by 2032, beyond an existing 2027 legal deadline.

articles.title: WHO chief urges US to lift Cuba fuel restrictions, warning of health effects
articles.summary: World Health Organization chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus urged the United States to lift its fuel restrictions on Cuba, warning that power shortages are harming hospitals and putting vulnerable people, including children, at risk. WHO pledged $2 million for immunization and medical equipment. Washington says food and medicine exports are exempt from sanctions; the wider effects of the fuel restrictions remain disputed.

articles.title: Yemen officials say strike on buses, trucks kills 26
articles.summary: An airstrike on a bus and trucks in Yemen’s Lahj province killed 26 people, including 14 civilians and 12 Houthi fighters, according to local officials cited by AFP. The Houthis blamed the Saudi-led coalition, while government forces said the Houthis carried out the attack. The conflicting accounts have not been independently resolved; the strike occurred near a front line advancing toward Aden.

articles.title: New film adaptation of the sacred Hindu epic Ramayana sparks debate over authenticity
articles.summary: The costly Indian film “Ramayana: Rise of a Legend,” released around Diwali, retells one of Hinduism's foundational epics with major Bollywood stars and Hollywood visual effects. It has become the highest-grossing Indian production in the United States, but viewers disagree over creative changes, including its portrayal of Ravana. A Hindu group has called for a boycott, while scholars note the epic has long had many regional and religious retellings.

articles.title: BepiColombo spacecraft remains safe in Mercury orbit after software glitch
articles.summary: Europe’s and Japan’s BepiColombo spacecraft remains safe in a stable orbit around Mercury after a software glitch prematurely ended its first thruster burn. The maneuver delivered about 77% of the planned velocity change, but the European Space Agency says the mission remains on track for the two science orbiters to separate on December 9. Routine observations are expected to begin in April 2027.

articles.title: CMS Announces Lower Negotiated Prices for 13 High-Cost Drugs
articles.summary: CMS announced negotiated prices for 13 high-spending Medicare Part B and Part D drugs, projecting $9.2 billion in net savings, or 45%, once the prices take effect Jan. 1, 2028. The medicines treat conditions including cancer and psoriatic arthritis. The announcement expands the federal negotiation program to 37 drugs across three cycles; actual savings for individual patients will depend on coverage, use and out-of-pocket rules.

articles.title: FCC plans vote to loosen local TV and radio ownership limits
articles.summary: The Federal Communications Commission plans to vote December 17 on replacing some local radio and television ownership limits with case-by-case reviews. Reuters reports the proposal would remove subcaps on AM and FM station ownership within local markets, while leaving restrictions on mergers among the four major broadcast networks unchanged. Supporters say broadcasters need scale to compete with streaming; critics warn consolidation could reduce local media diversity.

articles.title: FDA Approves First New Hormone Therapy for Early-Stage Breast Cancer in More Than 20 Years
articles.summary: The FDA approved giredestrant, marketed as Wilserdly, for certain adults with early-stage estrogen-receptor-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer after surgery. The agency said the daily oral hormone therapy is the first new treatment of its type for this setting in more than 20 years. Approval was based on a Phase 3 trial showing a 30% lower risk of invasive recurrence or death versus standard endocrine therapy; overall-survival follow-up continues.

articles.title: FDA Approves First Treatment for Limb-Girdle Muscular Dystrophy Type 2I/R9
articles.summary: The FDA approved Welgemda (ribitol) as the first treatment for limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 2I/R9, a rare inherited disorder linked to FKRP mutations. In a 112-person placebo-controlled study, patients showed improvements in walking speed and lung function at an interim analysis. The medicine is an oral solution for eligible adults and children weighing at least 30 kilograms; long-term outcomes and safety monitoring remain important.

articles.title: HKU Scientists Uncover Hidden Leaf Dynamics That Could Improve Amazon Rainforest Carbon Uptake Estimates
articles.summary: Researchers from the University of Hong Kong and collaborators found that seasonal leaf loss, renewal and ageing in the Amazon canopy are largely missed by conventional satellite observations. Accounting for those changes altered modeled annual photosynthetic carbon uptake by 9.4%, about 1.42 billion tonnes of carbon. The study suggests rainforest carbon estimates may need refinement; it does not mean the forest’s actual uptake changed by that amount.

articles.title: In the United States, more than 2.2 Million Women Relied on Fertility Awareness-Based Methods for Pregnancy Prevention in 2022-2023, Higher Than Earlier Estimates
articles.summary: New Guttmacher Institute and University of Utah estimates suggest 7%–8% of U.S. contraceptive users aged 18–44 used fertility-awareness methods in 2022–23, representing more than 2.2 million people. The researchers say standard surveys undercount users who combine cycle tracking with condoms or other methods. The estimates cannot establish a nationwide rise after 2023, though several Mountain West states showed growth through 2026.

articles.title: Massachusetts sues to block ICE courthouse arrests without judicial warrants
articles.summary: Massachusetts Attorney General Andrea Joy Campbell sued to stop ICE from making civil immigration arrests in state courthouses without judicial warrants. She says more than 1,110 courthouse arrests have occurred since President Donald Trump took office, including 38 after a state law took effect November 3. The Department of Homeland Security defended the practice as efficient; the court has not ruled on the new case.

articles.title: Moscow accuses Estonia of hostile actions on 'verge of triggering open war'
articles.summary: Russia accused Estonia of actions “on the verge of triggering open war” after Tallinn said it would close road crossings with Russia for six months from December 1. Moscow alleged Estonia allowed Ukrainian drones to use its airspace and obstructed Russian shipping; Estonia rejected the claims and said it never permits its territory to be used for foreign military operations. NATO said it was monitoring the situation.

articles.title: New York's top court shields social media companies from liability in Buffalo mass-shooting case
articles.summary: New York's highest court ruled 4-3 that major social media companies cannot be held liable in a lawsuit alleging their platforms helped radicalize the gunman who killed 10 Black people at a Buffalo grocery store in 2022. The majority said the attack was not a foreseeable consequence of platform design choices, applying Section 230 protections. A dissent said a jury should hear the claims; families are considering further options.

articles.title: Paper wasps recognize faces in ways strikingly similar to humans
articles.summary: Cornell researchers report that female northern paper wasps recognize individual faces using a localized group of neurons with activity resembling face-selective cells in primate brains. Experiments found the neurons responded to forward-facing images of other wasps, not side views or other insects, and encoded distinctive facial markings. The study suggests similar neural solutions evolved independently in insects and primates; researchers say comparisons with related wasp species may clarify how social recognition develops.

articles.title: PBS examines why some dogs watch and react to television
articles.summary: A PBS NewsHour report examined why some dogs watch television, focusing on a viral children’s series featuring animated seals. Veterinary ophthalmologist Freya Mowat said dogs can distinguish some colors and may respond to high-contrast movement and animal images; her research also studies age-related retinal changes. Not every dog enjoys screens: barking, agitation or escape behavior can signal that viewing is stressful rather than calming.

articles.title: Records: Government, judge debated constitutional implications of searching Rep. Ilhan Omar's home
articles.summary: Newly unsealed filings show a magistrate judge required federal investigators to account for Rep. Ilhan Omar’s constitutional privileges before searching her Washington home in October. The documents describe a protocol for protecting material covered by the Speech or Debate Clause but reveal little about the underlying investigation. Omar has not been charged and denies wrongdoing; most of the warrant affidavit remains sealed.

articles.title: Russia's return to international sport faces European resistance ahead of LA 2028
articles.summary: Russia's bid to return to international sport is meeting resistance from European governments and federations, complicating qualifying events for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. Norway, Sweden and Poland have denied visas to Russian athletes, while some teams refuse to compete against them. The Court of Arbitration for Sport is considering a Russian appeal over participation conditions, with a ruling expected by December 15; federations retain authority over many events.

articles.title: U.S. Senate panel investigates JD Vance's alleged role in Venezuelan oil deal
articles.summary: A Senate committee is examining whether Vice President JD Vance used his office to help commodities trader Vitol secure a lucrative Venezuelan oil contract. Senator Maggie Hassan requested records by Dec. 14 after Reuters reported a meeting with Vitol trader John Addison before the U.S. operation in Venezuela. Vance and Addison deny the meeting; flight records reportedly placed their aircraft at the same Montana airport.

articles.title: US, Mexico, Costa Rica, Jamaica awarded 2031 Women's World Cup, UK to host 2035 edition
articles.summary: FIFA appointed the United States, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica to co-host the 2031 Women's World Cup, while England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales will stage the 2035 tournament. The 2031 event will be the first senior Women's World Cup shared by four countries and the first with 48 teams. Both bids were approved unopposed at FIFA's extraordinary congress.

articles.title: War-related shipping disruption could put food aid for 7.3 million more people at risk, WFP warns
articles.summary: World Food Programme chief Luke Lindberg warned that conflict-related disruptions around the Black Sea, Strait of Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb could add $727 million to agency costs by mid-2027, threatening assistance for 7.3 million more people. The WFP has already cut its 2027 target from 110 million to 91 million recipients. A proposed humanitarian corridor for Russian and Ukrainian grain remains uncertain as attacks and shipping constraints persist.

articles.title: Board-game meetups draw adults seeking in-person friendships
articles.summary: In Denver, a board-game meetup that began as one man's search for players has grown into a twice-monthly gathering of more than 40 adults. Participants say games give strangers an easy shared activity and make conversation less awkward. The Associated Press reports that more than 900 board-game Meetup groups now operate across the United States, as people seek screen-free ways to build friendships and local community.

articles.title: Miley Cyrus marries drummer Maxx Morando in private California ceremony
articles.summary: Miley Cyrus married drummer Maxx Morando in a private California ceremony on November 21, Reuters reported, citing photographs posted by the singer and earlier reports from People and Entertainment Tonight. Cyrus shared black-and-white wedding images on Instagram; the couple have been together since 2021. Representatives did not immediately respond to Reuters, and details of the ceremony were limited.

articles.title: International UN talks on controlling use of autonomous weapons collapse
articles.summary: Negotiations in Geneva failed to secure a mandate for talks on a legally binding treaty governing autonomous weapons, after Russia objected and the UN forum’s consensus rule prevented agreement. More than 100 countries had backed stronger rules, while the United States and several other military powers favored nonbinding measures or reliance on existing law. Delegates adopted a weaker mandate to continue discussions, leaving regulation unresolved as such systems are already being developed and used.

articles.title: UN-backed talks extend AI killer robot discussions to 2028, no binding rules
articles.summary: UN-backed talks in Geneva ended with countries agreeing to continue work on lethal autonomous weapons for two more years and develop a possible accord by 2028. They did not commit to binding rules sought by the UN secretary-general and campaigners. Activists blamed major military powers for weakening the outcome; the International Committee of the Red Cross warned that autonomous weapons can behave unpredictably and urged human control over force.

articles.title: US pursuit of ‘Trump-class’ warships has blown cost of new fleet by billions, report warns
articles.summary: The Congressional Budget Office estimates the Navy’s 30-year shipbuilding plan will cost about $54 billion annually, 18% above Navy projections, with 15 proposed Trump-class battleships a major contributor. The report questions whether concentrating firepower in a few large vessels fits the Navy’s stated strategy. At the same time, the Iran war has extended deployments, delayed maintenance and strained readiness across the fleet.

articles.title: Denmark to expel Russian diplomat over alleged plot to kill US-Ukrainian rapper
articles.summary: Denmark said it would expel Russia’s defence attaché after police said they had disrupted an alleged Russian intelligence plot to kill US-Ukrainian rapper Kyivstoner before a September concert. Three suspects were arrested near the venue with firearms and knives, and a fourth was later detained; all denied wrongdoing. Moscow rejected the accusation, while Copenhagen said it was also considering tighter visa restrictions for Russian nationals.

articles.title: French police officers found guilty of racist assault on black music producer
articles.summary: Three French police officers were convicted of intentional group violence, with racism treated as an aggravating factor, after beating music producer Michel Zecler in Paris in 2020. Security-camera footage contradicted their account that Zecler had attacked them; the officers were also found guilty of falsifying an official report. They received prison sentences of one to two years, partly suspended, and were barred from police service for life.

articles.title: Man accused of sparking deadly Los Angeles wildfire found guilty
articles.summary: A federal jury convicted former Uber driver Jonathan Rinderknecht of arson charges tied to the January 2025 Palisades fire, which killed 12 people and destroyed thousands of homes and businesses. Prosecutors said he ignited a brush fire whose embers later reignited in powerful winds; Rinderknecht maintained his innocence and suggested fireworks caused the blaze. He remains in custody and faces a possible sentence of five to 40 years.

articles.title: Trump order requires federal contractors to coordinate with White House before responding to Congress
articles.summary: An executive order signed November 20 requires federal contractors and subcontractors to notify the White House and contracting agencies when Congress seeks information about their work with the executive branch. Contractors must coordinate responses and follow instructions to withhold material the administration deems privileged. The White House says this protects confidential operations; the order's effect on congressional oversight may be tested in court.

articles.title: A cyberattack using artificial intelligence targeted the EU in October, official says
articles.summary: The European Commission confirmed that an AI-assisted cyberattack targeting an EU institution was detected on October 22 and remained under investigation nearly a month later. Officials said several applications were temporarily taken offline and most have since been restored; they reported no evidence of a broad staff data breach. The attackers and full operational impact were not disclosed, leaving important questions about the intrusion unresolved.

articles.title: Record profits but record outflows: 'Sell Korea' trade stalks Seoul market
articles.summary: South Korea’s KOSPI has fallen 44% from its June record despite record AI-driven profits at Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix, erasing about 3.3 quadrillion won in market value. Reuters reported foreign investors were on track for a seventh consecutive month of net selling, with $115.2 billion in cumulative outflows. Analysts said waning confidence in debt-funded AI infrastructure and fading buybacks have left few buyers.

articles.title: South Korea becomes fourth country globally to hit $1 trillion exports on AI chip boom
articles.summary: South Korea’s exports passed $1 trillion for 2026, making it the fourth country to reach the milestone after Germany, the United States and China. Semiconductor shipments, driven by global AI investment, rose 184% in the first three quarters and represented 42% of exports. Reuters noted weak domestic demand and inequality remain concerns, prompting the government to plan a large fund for growth industries, young people and regional development.
